item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス21日（日本時間22日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が来季以降、開幕を打者でスタートさせる可能性が浮上した。アンドリュー・フリードマン編成本部長（49）がシーズン総括会見で、投球開始時期を含む新たな運用を大谷と模索していく考えを示した。また、今季悩まされた左膝、右上腕の患部について「手術の選択肢はない」と断言し、休養を経て復帰を目指すとした。
二刀流の再出発は、打席からになるかもしれない。大谷は左膝や右上腕の不調に悩まされ、万全の状態でポストシーズンを迎えることができなかった。シーズン総括の会見に出席したフリードマン編成本部長は、大谷の来季の起用について投打の始動時期も含め見直す考えを示した。
「彼が来年も投げると十分に見込んでいる。（運用面で）大きな要素の一つは、いつから投げ始めるか。開幕直後から投げるのか。そうであれば、最初の1カ月をどう管理し、その後にどう評価するか」
今季は3年ぶりに開幕二刀流で迎えたが、例年、打撃状態が上向く6月に左膝に違和感が発生。編成本部長は「不運にもモグラたたきのような状況になっていった」と説明。7月には右上腕にも違和感を覚えた。そうした1年を踏まえ、開幕二刀流を前提とせずにポストシーズンを見据えて〝投手開幕〟を遅らせるプランも示唆した。ただ、「しっかり腰を据えて話し合い、全体像を整理する必要がある」と大谷との対話を最優先にすると強調した。

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Dodgers reveal expectations for Shohei Ohtani’s 2027 comeback
item.dc:creator: Kyle Koster
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers fell short in their quest to pull off a rare threepeat as their journey ended in a four-game sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. There were many factors that led to the dissolution of their championship aspirations. The most visible was the unprecedented struggle of Shohei Ohtani, the best player in baseball, down the stretch and into the postseason. Ohtani encountered myriad issues during the year, including his left kn
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers fell short in their quest to pull off a rare threepeat as their journey ended in a four-game sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. There were many factors that led to the dissolution of their championship aspirations. The most visible was the unprecedented struggle of Shohei Ohtani, the best player in baseball, down the stretch and into the postseason.
Ohtani encountered myriad issues during the year, including his left knee and right shoulder—the latter kept him from pitching after July 3. A silver lining for the organization as it seeks to reload in the offseason is news today that the dual-threat star will not require surgery for those or any other ailments in the offseason.
Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman provided an update on Ohtani’s future on Wednesday. The major takeaway is that, with rest, the 2027 season is not expected to be impacted by those potential problems.
“I fully expect him to pitch next year,” Friedman told reporters.
For as great as Ohtani is, his skillset presents a unique challenge. There is no blueprint for how a player of his magnitude and versatility should best be deployed. Clearly, the Dodgers get high marks for maximizing his talents to this point.
Ohtani’s unique situation
“This is unprecedented, what he’s doing,” Friedman said. “So obviously for us, it’s unprecedented. We don’t have any experience to draw from. We can’t go look at how other situations have played out to try to learn from the good and the bad. We have to all just figure it out together. And I’m not only expecting him to pitch; we’re excited about him pitching. So now it’s about, ‘How do we do that? How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October?’ That’s a challenge.”
Though the Brewers are showing all the hallmarks of being a team of destiny, the Dodgers’ 2026 campaign will likely go down as a what-if. There’s no telling what would have happened had Ohtani not been a compromised version of himself at the season’s most pivotal moments.
The slugger went 4-for-22 with no extra-base hits in his first seven playoff games before hitting a homer in Game 4 against Milwaukee. That blast that proved to be too little and too late. Meanwhile, a spectacular start on the mound—where he went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA—was derailed and then ultimately shut down.
It will be fascinating to see how a once-in-a-lifetime player rebounds from the major disappointment. The Dodgers have to feel a bit better about the long-term outlook and clearer path back to the top the sport.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers' Dalton Rushing Undergoing Surgery That Will Cost Him Significant Time
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: Dalton Rushing stepped up big time for the Dodgers while Will Smith was out, but he, too, suffered injuries of his own. Rushing was placed on the injured list with right elbow inflammation in August, but returned in September. However, he was placed back on the injured list with right elbow discomfort. He was left off the postseason roster, and on Wednesday, The Los Angeles Times' Maddie Lee reported that he is undergoing elbow surgery. "Dodgers' Dalton Rushing is undergoing right elbow surgery
item.content:encoded:
Dalton Rushing stepped up big time for the Dodgers while Will Smith was out, but he, too, suffered injuries of his own.
Rushing was placed on the injured list with right elbow inflammation in August, but returned in September. However, he was placed back on the injured list with right elbow discomfort. He was left off the postseason roster, and on Wednesday, The Los Angeles Times' Maddie Lee reported that he is undergoing elbow surgery.
"Dodgers' Dalton Rushing is undergoing right elbow surgery today, per sources," wrote Lee. "It's expected to be a hybrid internal brace procedure. The expected timeline to return to catching full time is 9 months, with a return to hitting well before then."
When he was healthy, Rushing was a solid hitter for the Dodgers, proving why he was once a top prospect in the organization. However, his inability to play behind the plate while he recovers really limits the impact he can make.
It's not like the Dodgers can put him at designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani on the team. Even though he would be able to hit well before he could play as a catcher again, he may only be able to pinch-hit until then.
On top of that, the Dodgers have Smith. Rushing was already going to be pressed for playing time. Overall, the Dodgers will have to make some important decisions with Rushing down the line.
He is a good player, but as long as Smith and Ohtani are on the team, his role will always be limited.
More MLB: Aaron Boone Reveals Feelings On Managing Without Job Security Past 2027

item.title: [Heavy.com] Dodgers Announce Dalton Rushing Elbow Injury Update

The Dodgers’ second catcher on the roster tried to play through the injury as a designated hitter but never appeared in the postseason. Today, the Dodgers announced that Rushing will undergo surgery to address the elbow inju
item.content:encoded:
Following their disappointing elimination from World Series contention, the Los Angeles Dodgers announced an update on catcher Dalton Rushing.
Rushing, 25, was sidelined for the entire postseason with a partial tear of the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The Dodgers’ second catcher on the roster tried to play through the injury as a designated hitter but never appeared in the postseason.
Today, the Dodgers announced that Rushing will undergo surgery to address the elbow injury, Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times wrote.
“It’s expected to be a hybrid internal brace procedure. The expected timeline to return to catching full time is 9 months, with a return to hitting well before then,” Lee added.
Dalton Rushing’s Boosted Opportunity Derailed by Elbow Injury
The Dodgers’ second-year catcher got a new opportunity as the team’s primary catcher. The team gave him this chance while Will Smith was sidelined with a lingering neck injury that kept the Dodgers’ top catcher out for nearly three months.
Rushing was up for the new challenge. Before suffering the UCL tear, Rushing was batting .245/.335/.475 with 12 home runs and 36 RBIs.
Will Smith would finally return to the Dodgers lineup on Sept. 1. Meanwhile, the Dodgers’ depth at catcher remained limited as Rushing became unable to play defense.
The nine-month recovery period for Dalton Rushing goes in line with a return to catching in late July 2027. A return to batting will be significantly earlier for the 25-year-old.
Offseason Surgery ‘Not on the Table’ For Shohei Ohtani
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 15: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts after striking out against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game four of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium on October 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images)
Throughout the Dodgers’ 2026 season, the health status of superstar Shohei Ohtani was an ongoing conversation. For the first time since joining the franchise in 2024, the team sent Ohtani to the 15-day injured list at the end of the regular season.
The designation was due to right biceps inflammation, left knee discomfort, and a neck issue. The biceps and knee injuries surfaced earlier in the season, leading manager Dave Roberts to give him regular days off.
As the Dodgers won’t be the World Series Champion for the first time since 2023, the option for surgery to address the lingering setbacks is “not on the table,” says Dodgers president Andrew Friedman.
The Dodgers president also added that he fully expects Ohtani “to pitch next year.”
The 32-year-old was shut down from pitching in early July. In the limited opportunity on the mound, Ohtani finished the 2026 season as a pitcher with an 8-2 record, 1.79 ERA, and 0.95 WHIP across 85.2 innings.
After back-to-back 50-home-run, 100-RBI seasons, the injuries limited Ohtani to 30 home runs and 81 RBIs in 2026.
The Dodgers superstar said he “definitely” plans on pitching next season.
“And looking forward to having a better season next year,” Ohtani added.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Enough is enough. The Dodgers must stop letting Shohei Ohtani pitch
item.dc:creator: Bill Plaschke
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Shohei Ohtani’s two-way brilliance helped the Dodgers win two World Series titles and become a global draw, but his age and injuries are raising questions about the cost of pitching. - Ohtani says he plans to pitch next season, leaving the Dodgers with a difficult choice: find a way to manage his workload or consider a future without him. As they head into an offseason of overdue rest and roster reshaping, the Dodgers really only face one obstacle. But it
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
- Shohei Ohtani’s two-way brilliance helped the Dodgers win two World Series titles and become a global draw, but his age and injuries are raising questions about the cost of pitching.
- Ohtani says he plans to pitch next season, leaving the Dodgers with a difficult choice: find a way to manage his workload or consider a future without him.
As they head into an offseason of overdue rest and roster reshaping, the Dodgers really only face one obstacle.
But it’s a $700-million obstacle. It’s a 5,400-mile obstacle. It’s an obstacle whose gravitas can be found in everything from international sponsorships to stadium tours, an obstacle with expansive implications and crushing consequences.
The Dodgers have a Shohei Ohtani problem.
He is their best player… and their biggest pain.
He is insanely charming… and unrelentingly stubborn.
Dalton Rushing, who filled in for an injured Will Smith this season, had two stints on the injured list with a flexor strain in his right forearm, along with the UCL tear.
He has derived his worldwide popularity from his ability to hit and pitch with equal prowess, a deft duality unmatched in the history of baseball. This ability has helped earn him four MVP awards and status as the unofficial greatest player ever.
And, yeah, it’s made him very rich, setting him up to sign a 10-year, $700-million contract with the Dodgers based on the notion that he was not one, but two players, an All-Star hitter and an All-Star pitcher.
Three seasons later, he’s earned every penny, leading the Dodgers to two World Series championships while turning them into a global money machine, transforming this once staid organization into one of the most popular sports franchises in the world.
But, he’s changing. His body is changing. His skills are changing. He’s 32, with 13 seasons of professional baseball burdening his lumbering 6-foot-4 frame, and part of his game is slowly disintegrating under the weight.
The problem is his pitching. It’s hurting him. It’s distracting him. It’s exhausting him. His attempts to fix it on the mound led to a badly broken swing at the plate that may have caused the Dodgers to fail in their attempt at a three-peat.
And enough is enough.
This past season offered unassailable proof that Shohei Ohtani can no longer serve as both a full-time hitter and full-time pitcher. The Dodgers have no choice but to act on this truth and make a decision that is not only best for this team, but the long-term future of the organization.
They need to pull him off the pitching mound permanently. And if he insists on continuing this detrimental charade, they need to seriously consider trading him.
The Dodgers, after falling short of a three-peat in the NLCS, will look a little different next year. But is this the end of an era for the team?
Yes, yes, of course, trading Shohei Ohtani might be the dumbest move since the Boston Red Sox traded Babe Ruth. And, don’t forget, Ohtani has a no-trade clause that places him squarely in charge of his future here.
But at some point, if he insists on pitching despite the damage it is doing to his hitting and thus the entire team’s offense, the Dodgers may need to discuss other options with him.
Like, do what’s best for the team or take a hike.
The Dodgers, of course, are saying no such thing. Publicly, despite the hell he put them through, they are still backing him as a pitcher.
”I’m not only expecting him to pitch, we’re excited about him pitching,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman told reporters Wednesday at his postseason news conference. “The value of it is incredible, and so now it is incumbent on all of us to figure out the best way to do it.”
That’s going to require a lot of figuring, and it comes down to one seven-month task.
“How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October...that’s a challenge,” Friedman said.
Challenge? A better word might be, “Impossibility.”
For all of his optimism, Friedman hedged his bet when asked if it was possible for a pitcher at Ohtani’s age to survive an entire season and postseason as a two-way player.
“I don’t know the answer to that,” he said.
The answer, obviously, would be for Ohtani to walk into Friedman’s office this winter and tell him he’s done pitching and ready to win more MVP awards as a full-time hitter.
But so far, that’s not happening. That’s not even close to happening.
As of his locker-room interview immediately after the Game 4 sweeping by the Milwaukee Brewers last week, Ohtani still insists on pitching.
When asked a direct question about whether he planned to pitch next season, his answer was firm.
“Yes, definitely,” he told reporters through interpreter Will Ireton. “And looking forward to having a better season next year.”
He was also quite clear that he was unhappy ending the season off the mound, and will work on whatever adjustments are required to make sure that doesn’t happen again.
Major League Baseball is heading toward a turbulent offseason. There are four major things the Dodgers must address if they want to get back to the top.
“Not quite satisfied with how things shaped up on the pitching side at the end of the year,” he said. “This year, I haven’t pitched and I haven’t pitched in the postseason. You know, I haven’t been able to really come to grips in terms of what I’ve learned overall this season. It’s something that I’m going to kind of go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training program. and see what I can come up with for next season.”
Alas, there is no treatment for age. There is no training program for too many innings. There is nothing he can do to change the downward trajectory of his pitching career enough to save his hitting.
It’s not that he can’t pitch. In 14 starts this year he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA. If he devoted all of his time to pitching, he could easily win a couple of Cy Young awards to complement his four MVPs.
But since his second elbow surgery in 2023, he has yet to both hit and pitch in a full season. He strictly batted in 2024 while rehabbing from the surgery, then only started 14 games at the end of the 2025 season while the Dodgers slowly returned him to the mound.
Then came this season, which began with Ohtani openly pursuing a Cy Young Award while pitching at a Cy Young level.
But around midseason, his body began breaking down, the left knee, the right biceps, all of it hurting worse than he’d ever admit. He stopped pitching July 3 but kept working to return to the mound even while his hitting was declining from the constant effort.
The Dodgers should have shut him down in July and not allowed him back on the field in any capacity until he was fully healed. But they bowed to the wishes of their superstar, who insisted on continuing his unicorn quest even though it was clear that age and wear were finally taking its toll.
It was an organizational mistake that arguably cost them their season. He was finally pulled off the bullpen mound and yanked out of the lineup and placed on the injured list in September, but by then it was too late. Not only did he not pitch again, he stopped hitting, batting .192 in the postseason with four singles and a last-gasp home run.
The Dodgers aren’t the Dodgers without Ohtani creating chaos at the top of the order. They had won the previous two World Series titles on the shoulders of Ohtani the hitter, not Ohtani the pitcher.
Remember, he didn’t even pitch in the 2024 postseason, and in the 2025 postseason he recorded a 4.43 ERA in four starts, and yet they won both World Series championships
This current version of the Dodgers have proven they don’t need his pitching, but desperately need his hitting.
Now they need to convince him of that, and it won’t be easy. Being a two-way player is how he made his fortune. Being a two-way player is how he views his very identity.
Surely Ohtani saw this coming. His own father hinted at it in an open letter about his son after last season.
Shohei Ohtani showed the world a glimpse of his game-breaking abilities in Game 4 of the NLCS, but it was too little, too late for a Dodgers team that needs him healthy to challenge for a World Series title.
“ I believe the time will eventually come when he’ll focus on either pitching or hitting,” said Toru in a statement. “ If he can’t pitch anymore, I think he could do well as an outfielder. With practice, I’m sure he could handle it.”
Hmmm. The Dodgers could need a left fielder if they trade Teoscar Hernández as expected. Maybe Ohtani will accept surrendering the mound if he is handed a spot in the outfield?
No matter what happens, something has to happen, because what’s happening now is not working.
Shohei Ohtani as a two-way player has become a one-way ticket to disaster, and if he’s not willing to accept that reality, maybe he should be offered a one-way ticket out of Los Angeles.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dodgers ‘excited’ about Shohei Ohtani returning to the mound in 2027
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani’s days as a two-way player might have an expiration date. But the Dodgers agree with the four-time league MVP – that date hasn’t arrived yet. “I fully expect him to pitch next year,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said on Wednesday. “And I’m not only expecting him to pitch – we’re excited about him pitching. So now it’s about how do we do that? How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October? That’s a challe
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani’s days as a two-way player might have an expiration date. But the Dodgers agree with the four-time league MVP – that date hasn’t arrived yet.
“I fully expect him to pitch next year,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said on Wednesday.
“And I’m not only expecting him to pitch – we’re excited about him pitching. So now it’s about how do we do that? How do we manage through a long season and have him at his best going into October? That’s a challenge. And we have to figure that out together, and I’m confident that we will continue to learn from things as we go and continue to make it better.”
It was not a challenge Ohtani and the Dodgers were able to meet in 2026. Ohtani threw his last pitch on July 3 and the knee and biceps injuries that curtailed his pitching also impacted his hitting. His batting average (.275), on-base percentage (.377) and OPS (.889) were his lowest since his 2022 season with the Angels. His 30 home runs were his fewest in a full season since 2019 and he went a career-long 25 games without a home run before his three-run shot in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
Friedman said on Wednesday that Ohtani is not expected to require surgery this offseason to address the injuries – “just rest.”
“He’s had a lot of different things going on,” Friedman acknowledged. “Knee was bothering him off and on. It was just a little bit of an unfortunate game of whack-a-mole. The knee got to a better spot, and then just kind of the bicep area was bothering him. Just a number of different things. Some of it that would calm down for some period, some that would get re-irritated. It was just a lot of different things he was trying to contend with at once.”
Friedman said he expects Ohtani to be at full strength when the team reports for spring training next year – whenever that might be.
Ohtani will enter 2027 at age 32 and this year’s injuries might be an indication he cannot take on a two-way workload for a full season and the team will have to put on some significant limitations. Friedman indicated that is something the team has not decided yet.
“I don’t know the answer to that,” Friedman said.
“We’ll have to figure that out. We talked about this a lot. This is unprecedented what he’s doing. So obviously for us it’s unprecedented. We don’t have any experience to draw from. We can’t go look at how other situations have played out to try to learn from the good and the bad. We have to all just figure it out together.”
Even with Tarik Skubal headed to free agency, the Dodgers have starting pitching depth. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Roki Sasaki all return with Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Gavin Stone behind them. That could allow the Dodgers to be creative in limiting Ohtani’s time on the mound, preserving him for October and protecting his offensive contributions by delaying the start to his season as a pitcher, spacing out his starts or giving him more days off.
“We haven’t gotten into details yet,” Friedman said. “But I expect us to throw our heads together and figure out both in the batter’s box, on the mound, just how we marry all that together to have him impact us as much as he can during the regular season and then also be in a really good spot going into October. And so that’s what we’re going to try to figure out together.”
Managing Ohtani’s workload is only one thing Friedman and the Dodgers have to figure out on the heels of their four-game dismissal in the NLCS.
The Dodgers ended each of the past two years with the oldest position player group in MLB (by average age) and the younger, hungrier Milwaukee Brewers seemed to expose that.
“This isn’t something that we just woke up and were like, ‘Oh wow, the age of our position player group.’ We knew what things were going to look like in ’26, ’27, but also how talented these guys are, the way they prepare,” Friedman said.
In the past, Friedman has talked about the danger of big-market teams loaded with veteran players on high salaries “falling off the cliff” at some point. He does not see that cliff coming for the Dodgers any time soon thanks to a productive farm system.
“I think in a lot of ways it’s because you have an aging roster, and you have traded away prospects in your farm system to where you’re in the bottom 10 of farm system rankings,” he said of the trap other teams have fallen into. “That is why we have poured so much energy and focus into our farm system, because so much of avoiding that is having a talented wave of players who can come up and supplement around your core group of guys.
“We couldn’t feel more bullish on the position player core group that we have from A-ball through Triple-A that are coming. Obviously we’ve traded away a lot of really talented players also. So for us to be in that position, I think speaks to the incredible work of our baseball operations group with our scouting and player development and our baseball ops group of everyone working so well together. That is why it was such an important factor for us to not fall prey to the same thing that we’ve seen from a lot of large-revenue teams in the past, and we feel really good about our future outlook, and so now there’s an art to how to integrate and the timing of that and how to do it that we’ll spend a lot of time on.”
Josue De Paula is the most highly-regarded prospect in that wave of talent and the most likely to force his way onto the 2027 roster. He made his major league debut in September and was on the postseason roster for both series. But it’s clear he needs to improve defensively in order to become a viable option as an everyday player.
“We’ve talked through it, and he’s fully aware of continuing to improve defensively,” General Manager Brandon Gomes said. “We’ve all seen what he’s capable of in the box, which is incredibly exciting. … We’re not looking just to be like, ‘Oh, DePo got pretty good (defensively).’ I think his mindset and our coaching staff and all of us is to make him as good of a defensive outfielder as he can to be a full player because that’s what we expect of all of our guys that step on the field.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers’ Dalton Rushing undergoing elbow surgery, leaving 2027 role unclear
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Shohei Ohtani avoided surgery after his injury-plagued 2026 season. Dodgers backup catcher Dalton Rushing, however, wasn't so lucky. Rushing was set to undergo an internal brace procedure on Wednesday to address the damaged ligament in his right throwing elbow, according to multiple sources with knowledge of the situation. The operation will come with a nine-month timeline to return to full catching duties, as the Los Angeles Times first reported, but the expectation is that he could be ready as
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani avoided surgery after his injury-plagued 2026 season.
Dodgers backup catcher Dalton Rushing, however, wasn't so lucky.
Rushing was set to undergo an internal brace procedure on Wednesday to address the damaged ligament in his right throwing elbow, according to multiple sources with knowledge of the situation.
The operation will come with a nine-month timeline to return to full catching duties, as the Los Angeles Times first reported, but the expectation is that he could be ready as a hitter by the beginning of next season.
Rushing initially hurt his elbow at the beginning of August, while playing catch in the outfield before the start of a game. He spent much of the final two months of the regular season on the injured list, returning for only six days in early September before going down again when he suffered a setback in his throwing progression.
Rushing was healthy enough to be activated for hitting-only duties during the final week of the regular season. However, he did not make the team's postseason roster, bypassed by rookie sensation Josue De Paula as the team's left-handed bench bat in October.
Now, more uncertainty awaits Rushing, who is two years removed from his debut as one of the club's top prospects.
For all the strides he took in his second MLB campaign –– batting .246 with 12 home runs and 36 RBIs in 80 games, including an extended stint in June and July as the fill-in starter behind the plate during Will Smith's neck injury –– his place in the team's long-term plans remains unclear.
Rushing's surgery likely opens a pathway for Hunter Feduccia to begin next season in the backup catcher role, where he impressed as Rushing's replacement down the stretch this year.
Where Rushing will fit into the early-season roster is unknown.
Though he could still offer an option off the bench with his bat, there might be few opportunities for regular playing time with Shohei Ohtani entrenched as the designated hitter and Freddie Freeman at first base.
It's all just another setback for the 25-year-old slugger, who has yet to truly flourish at the big-league level.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers' latest Shohei Ohtani health update affirms he'll return to two-way status
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo

item.content:encoded:
Injuries derailed Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani's 2026 season. So much so that he stopped pitching in early July and hit only one home run after August 18. Ohtani finished the year with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts as a pitcher and a .275/.377/.512 slash line, .889 OPS, 30 homers and 81 RBI with just 11 stolen bases in 139 games as a hitter. This was Ohtani's worst offensive campaign since 2022 with the Los Angeles Angels.
Although Ohtani hit a three-run homer in Game 4 of the NLCS, the Dodgers were ultimately swept by the Milwaukee Brewers, missing out on winning their third consecutive World Series title. Ohtani struggled mightily at the plate in October, hitting .192 with a .631 OPS in eight games. Ohtani dealt with biceps and knee injuries, which hampered him in the final months of the regular season and playoffs.
Dodgers' Andrew Friedman shares update on Shohei Ohtani
With the Dodgers now eliminated, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman spoke to the media on Wednesday for the team's end-of-season press conference. During this press conference, Friedman revealed that surgery "is not on the table" for Ohtani this offseason.
He also shared another very telling update on Ohtani: Friedman expects Ohtani to return to being a two-way player next season.
There has been much debate as to whether Ohtani should quit pitching and only hit moving forward. But that's clearly not in the Dodgers' future plans, as they expect their star to re-enter their starting rotation next year. That being said, Friedman stated that Ohtani and the team would have to "put our heads together" to figure out his usage plan in 2027 and beyond next season.
When healthy, Ohtani looked like a Cy Young candidate this past season. There was much hype surrounding Ohtani's candidacy for the award early on in the year. However, injuries wiped out his chances after he was shut down from pitching in the beginning of July.
If Ohtani rejoins the Dodgers' rotation next season, he will pitch alongside Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Justin Wrobleski. The Dodgers are also hoping to re-sign Tarik Skubal, who will likely receive the largest contract for a starting pitcher in MLB history in free agency this offseason.
While it's certainly good news that Friedman and the Dodgers expect Ohtani to return to pitching next year, Los Angeles must make sure that their depth is fully loaded to minimize injury risk. And if Ohtani still doesn't look healthy, the team should make the decision to only use him as a hitter, given his bat is the most valuable aspect of his game.

item.title: [MLB.com] Ohtani won't need surgery, expects to return to 2-way form. How that looks is up in the air
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers are expecting Shohei Ohtani to be fully healthy by the beginning of the 2027 season. But after ongoing injuries derailed him in '26, they will have to evaluate what they can do differently to successfully get him through next year as a two-way player. Ohtani does not need surgery to address the right biceps and left knee injuries he has dealt with since at least June, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said at the Dodgers' end-of-season press conference o
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers are expecting Shohei Ohtani to be fully healthy by the beginning of the 2027 season. But after ongoing injuries derailed him in '26, they will have to evaluate what they can do differently to successfully get him through next year as a two-way player.
Ohtani does not need surgery to address the right biceps and left knee injuries he has dealt with since at least June, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said at the Dodgers' end-of-season press conference on Wednesday afternoon at Dodger Stadium.
Friedman added that he "fully" expects Ohtani to pitch in 2027, which is in line with what Ohtani said after the Dodgers' season came to an abrupt end when the Brewers swept them out of the NL Championship Series. But Friedman admitted to some uncertainty over whether Ohtani would be able to go through a full two-way regular season and still be at his best for a deep postseason run.
"We haven’t gotten into details yet," Friedman said, "but I expect us to throw our heads together and figure out both in the batter’s box, on the mound, just how we marry all that together to have him impact us as much as he can during the regular season and then also be in a really good spot going into October."
Ohtani hit a team-leading 30 homers with an .889 OPS and recorded a 1.79 ERA through 14 starts, but his ongoing injuries began to take their toll in midsummer. The 32-year-old did not pitch again after July 3 and saw his offensive production drop off steeply in mid-August, roughly around the same time he attempted to ramp back up on the mound.
It was not until September that Ohtani's injuries compromised him so badly that the Dodgers felt it was time to place him on the injured list. He still didn't look like himself when he returned and was a greatly diminished presence in the postseason, hitting 5-for-26 (.192) with one extra-base hit, a three-run homer in NLCS Game 4.
"I haven't been able to really come to grips in terms of what I've learned overall this season," Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton afterward. "It's something that I'm going to kind of go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training program, and see what I can come up with for next season."
Having Ohtani closer to full strength may not have changed the Dodgers' ultimate fate, as they were slumping up and down the lineup when their three-peat bid failed. But in order to sustain his ability to serve in a two-way role as he gets older, L.A. may need to manage him more proactively moving forward.
In 2027, the priority will once again be having a full two-way Ohtani in the postseason. To that end, one possibility the Dodgers are considering is that Ohtani might not start the season in the rotation, even if he is healthy enough to pitch at that point.
"I think so much of it is, when are we starting up both?" Friedman said. "Is he pitching right out of the gate? If so, how are we going to manage that in the first month and then assess things? … We're just going to have to be very deliberate about it on all sides, because the value of it is incredible, and therefore it's incumbent upon all of us to figure out the best way to do it."
Like with all aspects of managing Ohtani, piecing together the right plan will require an open conversation between all parties. That was a bit of an issue in 2026, when Friedman acknowledged that Ohtani may not have always accurately conveyed how he was feeling physically -- as most star players are wont to do in the interest of playing as much as possible.
"The greatest players we’ve been around all do the exact same thing," Friedman said, "and it’s rooted in how much he cares about competing and helping his team win."
Ohtani has never started a season as a two-way player and pitched in the postseason that same year. His biggest two-way workload was in his age-27 season in 2022, when he took 666 plate appearances as a hitter and threw a career-high 166 innings over 28 starts as a pitcher.
It's unclear whether Ohtani will be able to shoulder an equivalent two-way workload in a single season going forward. But his entire professional career has been defined by making the unprecedented possible. If he is to continue to do that going forward, he and the Dodgers will have to map out the blueprint to get there together.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Ohtani surgery 'not on the table': Dodgers chief
item.dc:creator: AFP ·
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday ruled out off-season surgery for Shohei Ohtani following the Japanese superstar's injury-hit end to the season. An ailing Ohtani's poor form was blamed as one of the key factors for the Dodgers' failed playoff campaign, which ended in a 4-0 series sweep to the Milwaukee Brewers last week. Ohtani, 32, had struggled with knee and biceps problems since July, and the Dodgers have faced scrutiny over their management of the four-time Most Valuable Player's injurie
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday ruled out off-season surgery for Shohei Ohtani following the Japanese superstar's injury-hit end to the season.
An ailing Ohtani's poor form was blamed as one of the key factors for the Dodgers' failed playoff campaign, which ended in a 4-0 series sweep to the Milwaukee Brewers last week.
Ohtani, 32, had struggled with knee and biceps problems since July, and the Dodgers have faced scrutiny over their management of the four-time Most Valuable Player's injuries leading into the playoffs.
But while some commentators have questioned whether Ohtani's grueling pitching and hitting workload was behind his dip in form, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday Ohtani would continue to pitch next season.
Friedman told reporters that surgery for Ohtani was "not on the table" as he described the star's injuries as a game of "whack-a-mole.
"He had a lot of different stuff going on," Friedman said of Ohtani. His knee was bothering him off and on.
"It was a little bit of an unfortunate game of whack-a-mole. The knee would get to a good spot and then the bicep was bothering him. It was a number of different things – some that would calm down for a period, some that would get re-irritated."
Ohtani, whose elite pitching and hitting talents have seen him acclaimed by some as the greatest player in baseball history, was believed to have been targeting a Cy Young pitching award in 2026 before his injuries left him unable to pitch.
Friedman said while the Dodgers wanted Ohtani to pitch next season, the team would develop a strategy that allowed their star player to reach the postseason in peak form.
"I'm not only expecting him to pitch, I'm excited about him pitching," Friedman said.
"So now it's a question of how do we manage a long season and have him at his best going into October. That's the challenge and we've got to figure it out together."
In statistical terms, Ohtani's figures in 2026 marked his worst since signing for the Dodgers in 2023.
After lashing 54 and 55 home runs in his first two regular season campaigns with the Dodgers in 2024 and 2025, Ohtani cracked only 30 homers this year.
His batting average dipped to .275, down from 2024 (.310) and 2025 (.282).
rcw/bb

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Have Clear Plan for Josue De Paula Amid Questions About His 2027 Role
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers need to find a position for their top prospect, Josue De Paula. After showcasing his potential as a hitter during a late-season call-up, it would surprise no one if the 21-year-old forced his way into the Dodgers' lineup in 2027. When Ohtani returned, De Paula was relegated to the bench. His ability (or rather, his in
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers need to find a position for their top prospect, Josue De Paula. After showcasing his potential as a hitter during a late-season call-up, it would surprise no one if the 21-year-old forced his way into the Dodgers' lineup in 2027.
The obvious question: where should he play?
De Paula slotted in at designated hitter when a multitude of injuries caught up with Shohei Ohtani in September. When Ohtani returned, De Paula was relegated to the bench. His ability (or rather, his inability) to improve the Dodgers' outfield defense was a major reason why.
“I think that he’s a young player," manager Dave Roberts said in September. "I mean, he’s 21 years old. His bat has certainly got him here, but it’s our job to make him value defense and get him to be a better defender.”
As a minor leaguer, De Paula saw time at all three outfield spots. But if Ohtani is healthy along with outfielders Teoscar Hernandez, Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker, there would appear to be no room for him in the Dodgers' 2027 lineup.
The Dodgers likely won't keep a rookie on their big league bench when playing time in the minor leagues is available next year. They also would be justified in finding a place for De Paula on their 26-man roster if his spring training performance mimics the .323/.500/.681 slash line he put up in 11 big league games to end the regular season.
The Dodgers worked with De Paula on his outfield defense during the regular season. That might not be possible during the offseason.
A lockout is expected to be imposed on Dec. 1, when the Collective Bargaining Agreement between MLB and the MLB Players' Association expires. Team personnel — managers, coaches, executives and others — were not able to contact 40-man roster players during the 2021-22 work stoppage. The same is likely to be true again.
That said, the plan for De Paula this offseason is clear.
"We've talked through it," Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said of De Paula on Wednesday at the end-of-season press conference. "His mindset, and our coaching staff and all of us is, to make him as good a defensive outfielder as possible."
President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman praised the impact of the Dodgers' clubhouse for embracing De Paula in September and October — as well as De Paula's development from 2025 to 2026.
As the Dodgers look to incorporate more prospects in the years to come, none might hold a more important place in the organization than De Paula.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.title: [mlb.com] Brewers have been MLB's best team under Pat Murphy. Can he lead them to a World Series win?
item.dc:creator: Adam McCalvy
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- How does the manager of one of Major League Baseball’s final four teams unwind when the workday is over and it’s the night before Game 1 of the National League Championship Series? If you’re Brewers skipper Pat Murphy, you coach. “It’s like the switch never goes off with him,” said Brewers radio broadcaster Lane Grindle. Grindle’s son, Luke, and Murphy’s son, Austin, are on a 12U team for Murphy’s Arizona-based Sandlot All Stars program, which has a partnership with the Hitters Base
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE -- How does the manager of one of Major League Baseball’s final four teams unwind when the workday is over and it’s the night before Game 1 of the National League Championship Series?
If you’re Brewers skipper Pat Murphy, you coach.
“It’s like the switch never goes off with him,” said Brewers radio broadcaster Lane Grindle.
Grindle’s son, Luke, and Murphy’s son, Austin, are on a 12U team for Murphy’s Arizona-based Sandlot All Stars program, which has a partnership with the Hitters Baseball Academy in Caledonia, Wis. Just as the Brewers were finishing their workout at American Family Field on the eve of the NLCS on Oct. 10, the boys and their teammates were beginning practice at Helfaer Field, a youth baseball facility right next to the ballpark on the former site of Milwaukee County Stadium.
Grindle looked up and saw Murphy in the stands. So, he coaxed him to come down to the field.
And in no time, Murphy was helping to run practice.
He watched bullpens and worked on some situational stuff on the infield, some baserunning, all of it,” Grindle said. “He’s a savant, he really is. I wish everybody could see him in that setting, because you get an incredible understanding of just how much he knows about the game.”
* * *
Coaching kids is one thing.
Coaching Major Leaguers is another, although Murphy has a knack for blurring the lines.
Take Game 4 of the NLCS. Third inning. The Brewers trailed, 4-0, after Shohei Ohtani hit a three-run moonshot in the Dodgers’ four-run second. Milwaukee hitters had started the game eight-up, eight-down against Tyler Glasnow. Things were not going well.
Murphy leaned in to offer nine-hole hitter David Hamilton a suggestion.
No other manager in baseball would deliver it this way.
“I told him, ‘Hammy, you’re not a good bunter, I know,’” Murphy said. “He did lead the Major Leagues in bunting for hits, but he’s not a great bunter -- yet. I said, ‘Look, put a bunt down today, and I promise you, you’re going to get pitches to hit the rest of the day.’”
Murphy’s thinking? Hamilton didn’t do much in the regular season against the Dodgers -- he was 2-for-14. They would be expecting a bunt. They would set up the defense and throw him good pitches to bunt. So, Hamilton dropped a bunt. It was not a good one. He became part of 10-up, 10-down to begin the game.
But sure enough, once the Brewers got the comeback started, Hamilton was right in the middle of everything. In the fifth, he hit an RBI single to make it 4-3 and knock Glasnow out of the game. Then he used his speed to steal second on Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips to open first base for Brice Turang to be intentionally walked. With the pressure on, Phillips walked William Contreras and was replaced by left-hander Alex Vesia, who walked Jake Bauers on four pitches to force in a run.
Poof, tie game.
And in the ninth against Edwin Díaz after the Brewers had the lead, Hamilton got another pitch to hit and delivered an insurance homer that sailed a Statcast-projected 402 feet. It was his first home run since Aug. 18.
Poof, Milwaukee wins.
The Brewers, led by their occasionally unorthodox manager, are going to the World Series. And they believe they have the team to win it.
“When people believe in themselves,” Murphy said, “that gives you the greatest joy you can ever believe.”
Murphy always believed he could manage in the Major Leagues if given the chance. For a long time it looked like he might not get one, despite big success as a college coach at stops including Notre Dame and Arizona State, where he went to the College World Series four times but left in 2009 amid an investigation of the program that eventually cleared Murphy of wrongdoing. He characterizes the whole ordeal as “a major injustice.”
So, he went to manage in the Minors for San Diego, and even got a callup to the Majors as interim skipper in 2015, only to be passed over for the full-time job. Today, Murphy sees that maybe he wasn’t ready. Maybe he was “still under construction” as a leader, as he likes to say.
“I made every mistake three times, and sometimes way more than that,” he said. “And most of it is well-intended, but a lot of it is ego. A lot of it is feeling like you have to have control. A lot of it is insecurity. So you want to make sure, double down, tell them three times.
“I think you learn as you get older and you learn that you're not that important, and be careful of that thing you have, which is authority. Don't use it as power. That's the danger.”
Through his mistakes, he believes he’s improved in that department. But there is work to do.
“I'm under construction,” he said. “For what it's worth, I'm still trying to figure it out.”
Here’s an example from early in his coaching career. Murphy has long had a soft spot for undersized players with heart, so it didn’t take long for him to love what a skinny infielder named Craig Counsell brought to Notre Dame in 1989. But he was a quiet kid, too quiet for Murphy’s liking. During indoor workouts over the winter, with Lou Holtz and the football team impatiently waiting to use the same field, Murphy instructed Counsell to yell, “MINE!” for every ground ball.
“I wanted him to stick his chest out and be a leader,” Murphy said. “There would be this shortstop out there yelling, ‘Mine!’ for every ground ball, and people would be like, ‘What the hell was that?’ But I was trying to bring it out of him, and he wanted to kill me.
“That was a mistake. He did just fine without yelling, ‘Mine!’ for ground balls. Had a pretty nice big league career.”
Murphy learned that you can’t force someone to be a leader -- a lesson that has served him well as soft-spoken Brewers captain Christian Yelich has grown into that role naturally over the past decade in Milwaukee. He arrived two years after Murphy, who came to town to be Counsell’s bench coach in 2016. When Counsell made a stunning departure for the Cubs after the 2023 season -- not stunning that it happened, but stunning that he went to Milwaukee’s chief rival -- the Brewers quickly identified Murphy as a candidate to take over.
It was not a given. Murphy was about to turn 65, and at the risk of sounding ageist, that was a consideration for a club stocked with young players. The more club officials talked to him about it, however, the more they came to understand he was the right man for the job.
“I think this was really, right place, right time for him,” said Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller, the GM who’d passed over Murphy in San Diego. “He had the trust of the team, of the organization. I think the experience he had with them, and then getting the job, put him in the right place to succeed. And he’s one of the best managers in the game.”
The Brewers have been the best team in the game since Murphy took the helm, with MLB’s highest winning percentage over the last three regular seasons. Instead of taking a step back after losing Counsell and former NL Cy Young Award winner Corbin Burnes in the same offseason, they were one win better in 2024 and won the division again. Then they set a franchise record with 97 wins in ‘25. Murphy won the NL Manager of the Year Award both years, the first Milwaukee manager to win the honor, which dates back to 1983.
After setting another franchise record with 103 wins in ‘26, he’s lined up to become the first manager ever to win that award three years in a row. Of course, Murphy credits the players. He likens himself to a chef, standing back to let things simmer.
“Sometimes your best move is to stay out of the way,” he said.
* * *
And then there are the times you want to really get in there and coach. Here’s a little story about that.
Luke Grindle was pitching a gem in an 11U championship game during the MLB All-Star break when Murphy leaned into Lane Grindle’s ear and said in a low voice, “Hey, he’s tipping his breaking ball. You might want to go talk to him about that.”
Grindle suppressed a smile.
But Murphy was serious.
“I go, ‘Murph, they’re 11. They’re not going to pick up on it,’” Grindle said.
Murphy’s response?
“You don’t know that!” he said.
It still makes Grindle laugh.
“His mind is incredible,” Grindle said.
* * *
At the end of Spring Training, Murphy made a presentation about his theme for the 2026 season. It was called, “Thread the needle.”
Nearly seven months later, standing on the field at Dodger Stadium, soaked in the beer and champagne that signified the Brewers had earned a trip to the World Series, he explained what that meant.
“When you thread a needle, OK, you take the little thread and you put it through that little hole. There’s not a lot of margin for error, you know?” said Murphy. “You have to be poised. It’s precise. And that’s what it takes to be the very, very best. So if you want to go beyond where we went [last] year with the best record in baseball, put yourself in that position again, and thread the needle.
“That’s exactly what the guys did. They would not be denied. Most teams get down 4-0 in a place like this, loud and crazy with their stars and we woke up their giant, he hits a three-run homer, most teams lay down. They just kept going, and that’s the beautiful thing about this group.”
They’re still going.
Game 1 of the World Series is Friday night.

item.title: [Heavy.com] New York Yankees Must Consider Signing Dodgers' 2X World Series Champion in Free Agency

One area of emphasis could be the bullpen, and left-handed relievers in particular might be a top item of need for a new-look Yankees squad. A very underrated bullpen option who is set to hit free agency is 2X World Series champion (with the Los Angeles Dodgers) Alex Vesia. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will be looking to enhance their roster during the 2026-27 offseason.
One area of emphasis could be the bullpen, and left-handed relievers in particular might be a top item of need for a new-look Yankees squad.
A very underrated bullpen option who is set to hit free agency is 2X World Series champion (with the Los Angeles Dodgers) Alex Vesia.
Vesia has been a very solid southpaw reliever for the past several years with the Dodgers, and if the Yankees can just meet his contract demands, he would be a great fit in the Bronx.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Cy Young Pitcher Set for MLB Free Agency
Why the Yankees Should Sign Alex Vesia…
While the Los Angeles Dodgers might make a strong run to retain their southpaw reliever Vesia, considering he’s on the open market for the first time in his career, there’s sure to be a lot of suitors and options for Vesia.
Vesia is coming off a 2026 campaign where he posted an ERA of 2.64 over 58 IP, and 74 strikeouts.
Former Dodgers pitcher Alex Vesia would be an excellent fit for the Yankees, providing a proven left-handed reliever with postseason experience and providing value matchup flexibility.
With Brian Cashman recently getting extended, he might be trying to make a splash in free agency, and Vesia would be a great value signing.
Another thing to note is the Yankees will likely feature a brand-new bullpen in 2027 with several of their 2026 members also hitting free agency.
More MLB on Heavy: Shohei Ohtani Sends Out 2-Word Appreciation Post After Los Angeles Dodgers Abrupt Playoff Exit
Alex Vesia Has Been Solid Throughout His 7-Year Career
Alex Vesia has posted very solid stats throughout his 7-year MLB career.
He debuted with the Miami Marlins in 2020, but quickly joining the Dodgers after that, where he’s spent the last six seasons of his career.
Across 332.1 IP in seven seasons, Vesia carries an ERA of 2.87 with 16 saves, a pWAR of 5.7, and 443 total strikeouts.
In 66.1 IP in 2024 with the Dodgers, Vesia boasted an ERA of 1.76.
New York Yankees fans, is Alex Vesia a free agent that you would like to see the front office pursue??

item.title: [サカノワ] 【MLB】大谷翔平のドジャースも影響? トランプ大統領がロックアウトを予測「起きるだろう」、ワールドシリーズは「誰も気にしていない」

item.content:encoded:
【MLB】大谷翔平のドジャースも影響? トランプ大統領がロックアウトを予測「起きるだろう」、ワールドシリーズは「誰も気にしていない」
北中米W杯抽選会での米国トランプ大統領。(Photo by Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)
12月1日に労使協定が期限切れ。サラリーキャップ導入を巡り対立
アメリカのドナルド・トランプ大統領は10月20日、米大リーグ（MLB）で懸念されるロックアウトについて、「起きるだろう（That is going to happen）」との見通しを示した。一方、ワールドシリーズに関する質問には「誰も気にしていない（Nobody cares）」と答えた。米スポーツメディア『The Comeback』が報じた。
記者からロックアウトの可能性について尋ねられたトランプ大統領は、「そうなると思う。起きるだろう」と回答。その後、ワールドシリーズに進出したチームの年俸総額について質問されると、「分かった、また別の機会にしよう。誰も気にしていない」と述べたという。
MLBでは、球団側と選手会の現行労使協定が2026年12月1日に期限を迎える。次期協定を巡る大きな争点の一つが、サラリーキャップ（年俸総額の上限）の導入だ。球団側が導入を求める一方、選手会は反対している。
米メディア『アクシオス』も10月20日、今季のワールドシリーズがミルウォーキー・ブルワーズとタンパベイ・レイズの対戦となり、ロックアウトを巡る労使対立が焦点になっていると報じた。両チームは高額年俸を投じる球団とは異なる運営で勝ち上がっており、サラリーキャップ導入を巡る議論にも影響を与えている。
一方、大谷翔平が所属するロサンゼルス・ドジャースも、今後の労使交渉の影響を受ける可能性がある。ロックアウトに至れば、選手との契約や球団施設の利用などが制限され、オフシーズンの補強や2027年シーズンの準備に影響が及ぶことも考えられる。
トランプ大統領は以前からサラリーキャップの導入を支持する考えを示している。労使交渉が合意に至るかどうか、MLB各球団と選手会の動向が焦点となる。

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani Admits He Was Exposed by Brewers in NLCS
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' performance in the 2026 National League Championship Series was a stark contrast to their 2025 appearance. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' performance in the 2026 National League Championship Series was a stark contrast to their 2025 appearance.
The Dodgers dominated every way they could in 2025 against the Milwaukee Brewers, sweeping them in four games.
Before the 2026 NLCS, the Brewers vowed that this matchup would be different, and they backed that up. Milwaukee returned the favor, sweeping the back-to-back champions in dominant fashion.
It was a complete 180 in this year's NLCS, and that goes for Shohei Ohtani's play, too.
Ohtani struggled throughout the second half of the season, and those issues carried into the postseason. The 32-year-old had a difficult playoff run, with the Brewers exposing his struggles even further.
After the loss, Ohtani acknowledged that Milwaukee had "exposed" him and gave the Brewers credit for doing so.
"The Brewers were overall strong and a very good team, and it really exposed some of the parts of me as a player, and got to give some credit to that," Ohtani said through his interpreter.
Dodgers’ Hopes for Shohei Ohtani’s Recovery Fell Short in the Postseason
Ohtani hit .230 in the NLCS, getting a three-run home run in Game 4 and close to nothing else.
His overall postseason numbers were even worse, as he hit .192 with that one home run, three RBIs and an OPS of .631 while striking out 10 times in 26 at-bats over eight games.
The four-time MVP was a shell of himself, largely because of lingering injuries that weren't properly addressed during the regular season.
Ohtani was dealing with a combination of left knee irritation and right biceps tightness. His knee injury flared up in late June, and his right biceps tightness popped up multiple times throughout the year.
Ohtani's offensive decline began around mid-August and continued through his rough stretch into October. He didn't get enough time to return to his average form, as he played through those injuries until he hit the injured list in September.
The Dodgers hoped that those two weeks off would help him get to a better place, but that was more wishful thinking. Ohtani was never the same, and it was clear it hurt the Dodgers in the long run.
Will Shohei Ohtani Need Surgery to Address His Injuries?
Ohtani was noncommittal about potentially undergoing surgery this offseason.
“Hard to tell at this point,” he said. “It’s something that’s going to be analyzed, discussed over the offseason, and [we’ll] see if it’s a viable thing to do.”
What he did make clear, however, is that he plans on continuing his two-way play in 2027.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.content:encoded:
ドジャースの大谷翔平は今季のレギュラーシーズン途中より、故障に悩まされ続けた。開幕から「二刀流」で出場し、投手では8勝（2敗）をマークするも、前半戦でマウンドを離れている。
【写真】ドジャース奥様会「今日も素敵なスマイル」の真美子さんをチェック　大谷翔平が今PS初本塁打！エール届いた
右上腕二頭筋の張り、さらに左膝も痛めたことで、7月3日のパドレス戦での先発が最後の登板となった。両箇所の故障はその後も長引き、投手での復帰を断念する決断も下され、さらに9月には試合欠場を経て、負傷者リスト（IL）に登録される事態に。シーズン残り5試合で復帰を果たした大谷は、今季の打撃成績を打率.275、30本塁打、81打点、OPS.889などの数字で終えている。
戦列復帰以降、ポストシーズンも含めバッティングも復調とはならず、ブルワーズとのナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ4戦目で58日ぶりとなる本塁打を放ったが、チームはシリーズ4連敗で敗退。予想外の苦戦は、主砲の不振も少なからず影響したことは間違いない。
チームの目標だった世界一3連覇を逃し、大谷自身も怪我で思うような結果を残せなかった今シーズン。メジャー公式サイト『MLB.com』では、10月19日配信の大谷の特集記事の中で、「オオタニは、重要な時期に打撃不振に陥ったドジャースの複数の打者の1人だった」と評している。さらに、その原因となった右腕、左膝の故障については、「球団側、そしてオオタニ自身も、もっと適切に対処できた可能性があったのでは」などと指摘。
同メディアは、「ドジャースは時折、オオタニの健康状態について先手を打った対応も取っていた。投手としての負担と打者としての負担を分けて管理したり、登板翌日には完全休養日を設けたりしていた」と球団側の対応を振り返る。だが、その一方で、「しかし、身体に明らかな問題が生じていることがはっきりするまでは、先発登板を回避させることも、負傷者リストに登録することもなかった」と訴えている。
不調を抱えていた大谷をシーズン終盤までプレーさせていた球団の判断に疑問を投げかける同メディアは、記事の最後で「もし、オオタニの今シーズンの結末を変えることができたとすれば、それは故障に苦しみ始めた初期の段階で、球団側がもっと積極的な対応を取ることだったのかもしれない」と結論付けている。
ポストシーズンでの戦いを終えた直後、大谷は引き続き二刀流でグラウンドに立つ意向を示していた。今季の苦い経験を踏まえ、ドジャースがどのようなコンディション管理を行うのかにも、大きな注目が集まる。
[文/構成:ココカラネクスト編集部]

item.content:encoded:
By now, it's been like a week since the Los Angeles Dodgers were eliminated from the MLB playoffs.
That means the 2026 World Series is set, with the Milwaukee Brewers taking on the Tampa Bay Rays in the Fall Classic.
Who knows how far the Los Angeles Dodgers could have gone in the MLB playoffs if Shohei Ohtani wasn't dealing with a handful of injuries/enduring a gnarly slump.
That said, Ohtani still took some time to send out a quick appreciation post.
More MLB on Heavy: Philadelphia Phillies Trade Prediction Lands 2X All-Star Outfielder
Shohei Ohtani Makes Quick Social Media Post
In the week following the Los Angeles Dodgers' elimination from the MLB playoffs, Shohei Ohtani made the following 2-word appreciation post, with the caption:
"Thank you"
Some fans in the comments are very glad/excited that Shohei Ohtani is finally able to get some rest, as the past three years have been Go, Go, Go for Ohtani.
It's been reported that Ohtani has been dealing with a knee/biceps injury during 2026, and there's a possibility that Ohtani will undergo offseason surgery.

item.content:encoded:
How Dodgers can best utilize Josue De Paula with Shohei Ohtani problem originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
For the first time since 2023, the Los Angeles Dodgers will not be crowned Major League Baseball's champion.
Surely, the NL West organization will be looking to end up back on top next year with a few minor roster adjustments.
Most of the Dodgers' roster is expected back in 2027, including, of course, Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter.
Top prospect Josue De Paula could play a larger role, but the Dodgers may have to clear space in the outfield.
"There admittedly isn't much that the Los Angeles Dodgers can do other than hope for better years from their core position players, but one thing they can and really must do is clear room for Josue De Paula," FanSided's Zachary Rotman wrote.
"DH is probably De Paula's best position, but with Shohei Ohtani taking up that spot for the long-term future (and rightfully so), the Dodgers need to find room for their 21-year-old phenom in the corner outfield," he added.
In a small sample size of 42 plate appearances, De Paul hit .323 with a homer and three doubles. Facing MLB pitching for the first time, he walked six more times (11) than he struck out (5).
Rotman suggested the Dodgers contemplate moving on from one of their corner outfielders, but it probably won't be Kyle Tucker.
"Many Dodgers fans would probably love for the team to trade Kyle Tucker away after his wildly disappointing debut season in L.A., but given his contract, the odds of that happening are slim to none," Rotman wrote. "That leaves Teoscar Hernandez as the player likeliest to get dealt, or at least placed in a short-side platoon role, with De Paula playing most of the time against right-handed pitching."
If the Dodgers can find a trade suitor for Hernandez, that would leave De Paula as their likely everyday left fielder and more room for the 21-year-old to grow.

item.title: [abc7.com] Where 2026 ranks among best World Series matchups since 2000
item.dc:creator: David Schoenfield
item.description: This year's World Series will have a tough act to follow. Not only was the 2025 World Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays the first seven-game affair since 2019, but it featured an 18-inning game and then a Game 7 that might have been the greatest baseball game ever played.
