item.content:encoded:
Much of the media's attention heading into this year's NLCS rematch between the Milwaukee Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers was on the strength of the defending World Series Champions' starting pitching group. With a pair of Cy Young-winning left-handers in Tarik Skubal, whom the Dodgers acquired at the midseason trade deadline, and Blake Snell, as well as 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto and All-Star right-hander Tyler Glasnow in their rotation, that attention was well-deserved.
However, through the first three games of the NLCS, the Brewers have bested Los Angeles' top three starters and built a commanding 3-0 series lead. Skubal and Snell took the loss in Games 1 and 3, respectively, and sandwiched in between was a 2.2-inning, 75-pitch start from Yamamoto that forced Dave Roberts to use seven relief pitchers in Game 2. On the other side, Milwaukee's starting group hasn't necessarily been the strength of their pitching staff during the postseason -- that would be their bullpen -- but the trio of Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson, and Robert Gasser combined for 13.1 innings and allowed just two earned runs through the first three NLCS games.
Game 4 is where things get interesting. While the Brewers' decision to start Miz, Henderson, and Gasser in the first three games of the NLCS felt like an obvious one, especially after Gasser's strong showing in the NLDS, who would get the ball to start Game 4 remained an unanswered question through this morning.
However, just moments ago, the Brewers officially revealed that rookie southpaw Shane Drohan will start Game 4 of the NLCS tonight. Drohan, who will be making his postseason debut, will be the first out-getter of Milwaukee's quest for never-before-seen level of redemption in a playoff series.
Brewers trying to become first team in MLB history to sweep a team in the playoffs who swept them in the previous postseason
The Brewers just have to win one of their next four games to return to the World Series for the first time since 1982. That much is true. That said, closing out the Dodgers tonight and completing one of the most impressive sweeps in postseason history would be a redemption performance never before seen in MLB history. According to MLB.com's statistician Sarah Langs, no team in the history of MLB has swept a team in a postseason series after being swept by that same team in the previous playoffs.
After the demoralizing loss that the Brewers suffered in last year's NLCS, defeating the Dodgers in four games this year would easily be one of the most satisfying postseason series sweeps in MLB history. Pair that with the payroll disparity that exists between the two clubs, the fact that Los Angeles is pursuing a three-peat, and the Dodgers' victory in the Tarik Skubal trade deadline sweepstakes, and the Brewers sweeping MLB's Evil Empire would be especially gratifying.
Completing that sweep in Game 4 tonight starts with a strong showing from Drohan, who hasn't pitched in any of the Brewers' first seven postseason games this year. Drohan impressed during the regular season, with a 4.19 ERA in 124.2 innings to prove it. His low arm-slot from the left side matches up well with Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman, and his six-pitch mix should keep the struggling Dodgers' offense off-balance.
It likely won't be a long start for Drohan, especially given the arms available in Pat Murphy's 'pen. In theory, only DL Hall is unavailable for tonight's game, but the Brewers may elect to avoid using Abner Uribe for an eighth consecutive game as well. However, that leaves Kyle Harrison, Dustin May, Chad Patrick, Aaron Ashby, Antonio Senzatela, JoJo Romero, and Trevor Megill available for Murphy to turn to after Drohan.
Any type of victory over the Dodgers in this year's NLCS would represent redemption for the Brewers after being swept by Los Angeles a season ago. However, Milwaukee's only shot at historic redemption that has never occurred in the history of MLB is tonight, during which rookie southpaw Shane Drohan will kick off their sweep attempt.

item.title: [si.com] Brewers Are Using Postseason Stage to Showcase MLB’s New Era
item.dc:creator: Tom Verducci
item.description: Los Angeles — When dynasties fall, it is not insurrection, nor jealousy, nor sloth that bring them down. It is the undefeated champion of the world, Father Time. We are watching the Los Angeles Dodgers age out. The Milwaukee Brewers proved for a third time in the National League Championship Series they are the better (and younger) team, completing a beautiful triptych of comebacks with a 6-2 win in Game 3 on Wednesday. In three successive games, the Dodgers had Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles — When dynasties fall, it is not insurrection, nor jealousy, nor sloth that bring them down. It is the undefeated champion of the world, Father Time. We are watching the Los Angeles Dodgers age out.
The Milwaukee Brewers proved for a third time in the National League Championship Series they are the better (and younger) team, completing a beautiful triptych of comebacks with a 6-2 win in Game 3 on Wednesday. In three successive games, the Dodgers had Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell on the mound with a lead and lost all three. Ninety-five million dollars, four Cy Young awards and a World Series MVP worth of pitching and they could not hold back Milwaukee any more than you can hold back water with your hands.
But the most obvious reason why the Brewers have put the Dodger dynasty on the brink of extinction is this: the youngest pitching staff in baseball—and the hardest throwing staff in postseason history—has smothered the oldest team in baseball. Milwaukee is pushing around the aging Dodgers lineup with a barrage of fastballs in three versions, especially power sinkers. They are shoving 66.8% fastballs at the Dodgers at an average velocity of 97.9 mph. The Dodgers’ only path to victory is to slug and the Brewers simply won’t allow it.
“I just think they’re really good pitchers,” Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas said. “A lot of their pitchers throw three different fastballs. They throw hard, and they’ve been locating the ball really well. They haven’t really given us too much of an opportunity to kind of build momentum.
“They’ve been attacking the zone. They throw their stuff in the zone—and with all three fastballs. A lot of guys have a cutter, a sinker and a four-seam fastball. It’s really hard to put barrels on the ball.
“At the end of the day, it’s just the velocity of their stuff. They throw the ball really hard. And we all know when you throw that hard, it’s really hard.”
The Brewers knew coming into the series that in today’s game older players don’t hit elite fastballs as well as younger players, and so the matchup was to their liking. But this? Who could have seen this in the NLCS? The Dodgers:
- Have two extra-base hits in 105 plate appearances
- Have been outhomered, 5-0
- Are the first team in franchise history to lose three straight games in one postseason with no home runs and no attempted stolen bases
- Are hitting .228 against fastballs
- Are 2-for-16 with runners in scoring position, part of a 3-for-32 postseason disaster in those spots
This has been the year in which baseball made a sharp turn when it comes to the speed of the game. Younger players thrive. Velocity, and the widespread adoption of the family of three fastballs, changed everything. You need fast-twitch athleticism, youthfulness. You need this generation of players who know velocity as a first language. You need rangy players on defense. The numbers bear out that younger players are the preferred way to go.
Players 30 and younger this year hit .247. Players in the 31-35 year-old demographic hit 10 points worse, .237, their worst showing ever. There was a time when front offices valued those 31-35 players because it seemed to be the peak intersection of experience and physical tools. Front offices were afraid to commit to younger players because of the lack of reps and track records. Those days are over.
The difference on the field in NLCS Game 3 was striking. The Brewers are the fastest team in baseball, as measured by sprint speed. The Dodgers are 24th.
The Brewers started a lineup and a pitcher with an average age of 26.1. They became the first team in history with a second postseason game starting three players 22 and younger: leftfielder Jackson Chourio, shortstop Cooper Pratt and rightfielder Luis Lara. Chourio opened the game with a first-pitch homer. Pratt smacked three hits, stole a base and scored a run. Lara flew around rightfield like a bird of prey, snaring anything that dared enter his airspace.
Watching Chourio, 22, Garrett Mitchell, 28, and Lara, 21, patrol the outfield was like watching an Olympic sprint relay team.
On the other side of the field, the Dodgers, especially their bats, looked old and slow. The average age of their starting 10 was 32.3 years old—more than six years older than Milwaukee’s fearless group. Only two starting Dodgers were in their 20s: centerfielder Andy Pages, 25, and Kyle Tucker, 29, who with his diminished range and baserunning has been trending older than his age.
By starting eight players 31 and older, these Dodgers joined the 2023 Dodgers, who got bounced by the Diamondbacks, as the only teams in the past 19 postseasons to trot out so many starting players that old in a game.
Fittingly, the old team played an outdated style of baseball, one from a generation ago. The ninth-place hitter, Tommy Edman, twice batted after the leadoff runner reached first base. Twice manager Dave Roberts did not ask him to bunt.
“I thought about it, but it’s just, he had a good pitch to hit. Flew out,” Roberts said. “I just didn’t feel giving up an out right there. Early in the game, I wanted Tommy to hit ...
“We haven’t been getting hits with runners in scoring position. To give up an out, to bank on getting a hit with runners in scoring position, I’d rather just try to maybe slug, hit a double.”
Edman was a below average hitter (97 OPS+) with a .385 slug this season.
Roberts and the Dodgers keep waiting for slug to show up at the expense of forfeiting the situational baseball as deployed by the other three remaining teams, the youthful Brewers, Guardians and Rays. The Dodgers still may be waiting Thanksgiving morning.
For instance, the Dodgers were down 1-0 in the sixth when Roberts sent 36-year-old Max Muncy to hit for Pages with runners on first and second and no outs. In that situation, the Brewers are bunting. Milwaukee plays get-em-over, get-em-in ball. The Dodgers? No way. Muncy is a three-true outcome guy. He is not going to bunt. Again, the Dodgers played for slug and got nothing. Muncy struck out. Will Smith, 31, did save the rally with a two-run double. But the Dodgers would go 1-for-12 after that against hard-throwing relievers D.L. Hall and Trevor Megill.
The lineup remained cold. Shohei Ohtani, 32, cannot pull a baseball because of lower-half injuries that won’t allow him to properly turn his hips and get to a firm front side. Freeman, 37, has three extra-base hits since Aug. 31.
“[Our] pitching staff has been great, to be honest,” Rojas said. “It’s really hard to put it into context when you have to pitch and have to play defense with a one run lead every single time. It’s like asking these guys to just throw a perfect inning every single time. It’s not sustainable. So, the blame is on the offense. We all know we could’ve done better, but nothing we can do now.”
How in the world has Milwaukee made Los Angeles look so bad?
“It’s pretty simple,” Muncy said. “We’ve played like [poop]. They’ve played great.”
Occam’s razor (or commode) aside, the one-sided NLCS is bigger than that. It stands as a changing of the guard, recalling the 1964 World Series, when the St. Louis Cardinals, emblematic of the National League embracing Black and Latin American players, ended the dynasty of an aging New York Yankees team, then the second oldest team in baseball. The younger, faster, harder-throwing, more creative team has been, beyond doubt, the better team.
Tom Verducci is a senior writer for Sports Illustrated who has covered Major League Baseball since 1981. He also serves as an analyst for FOX Sports and the MLB Network; is a New York Times best-selling author; and cohosts The Book of Joe podcast with Joe Maddon. A five-time Emmy Award winner across three categories (studio analyst, reporter, short form writing) and nominated in a fourth (game analyst), he is a three-time National Sportswriter of the Year winner, two-time National Magazine Award finalist, and a Penn State Distinguished Alumnus Award recipient. Verducci is a member of the National Sports Media Hall of Fame, Baseball Writers Association of America (including past New York chapter chairman) and a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 1993. He also is the only writer to be a game analyst for World Series telecasts. He lives in New Jersey with his wife, with whom he has two children.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Reveal Lineup As They Aim to Extend Season Past Game 4
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers set their lineup for their NLCS Game 4 matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers set their lineup for their NLCS Game 4 matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday.
The Dodgers currently face a 3-0 deficit in the series, and need to win Thursday’s game to keep their World Series hopes alive. They managed just two runs in Game 3 of the NLCS, the first of three potential games in Los Angeles.
Who is Pitching For the Dodgers?
As they announced before the start of the series, the Dodgers have Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the fourth game of the NLCS. Injuries cut Glasnow’s regular season short, allowing him to make just 22 starts while posting a 3.49 ERA, but he earned an all-important win for the team in Game 4 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.
He threw 4.2 innings while allowing just one earned run, though he allowed five walks in the process. The veteran right-hander will look to keep the Brewers off of the board to give the Dodgers some kind of advantage in Thursday’s game.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
The Dodgers made just one substitution in their lineup from Game 3, but drastically changed the order in which their hitters appear. Shohei Ohtani returned to the top of the lineup as the Dodgers’ designated hitter, followed by shortstop Mookie Betts and first baseman Freddie Freeman. Catcher Will Smith, after his two-run double in Wednesday’s loss, returns to the cleanup spot for the Dodgers, and right fielder Kyle Tucker follows him to the plate.
Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez will bat sixth, and Miguel Rojas remains in the lineup, though as the second baseman for Game 4. Batting eighth is center fielder Andy Pages, and Kiké Hernandez steps in at third base to round out the lineup.
Dodgers’ Lineup vs. Braves
1. Shohei Ohtani, DH
2. Mookie Betts, SS
3. Freddie Freeman, 1B
4. Will Smith, C
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
7. Miguel Rojas, 2B
8. Andy Pages, CF
9. Kiké Hernandez, 3B
P. Tyler Glasnow, RHP.
When Does Thursday’s Game Start?
First pitch for Thursday’s game comes at 5:00 p.m. PT, moved up one hour from the original start time of 6:00 p.m. PT due to scheduling changes in the ALDS. The Dodgers will look to generate some offense and extend their season with a strong performance in Game 4.

item.title: [The Times of India] Josue De Paula’s emotional MLB debut: How his father Josue De Paula Sr. and grandmother Sixtra Brito De Paula helped shape his MLB journey to the LA Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk
item.description: For Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula, what was to be his professional breakthrough turned out to be his MLB debut on September 11, 2026, and the 21-year-old hugged his father, Josue De Paula Sr., who came from New York to Miami to see his son in the majors, before taking the field against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park. His grandmother, Sixtra Brito De Paula, was also on hand to celebrate the accomplishment. Their presence was a reminder of the family ties that helped De Paula go
item.content:encoded:
For Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula, what was to be his professional breakthrough turned out to be his MLB debut on September 11, 2026, and the 21-year-old hugged his father, Josue De Paula Sr., who came from New York to Miami to see his son in the majors, before taking the field against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park.
His grandmother, Sixtra Brito De Paula, was also on hand to celebrate the accomplishment. Their presence was a reminder of the family ties that helped De Paula go from a young baseball enthusiast to one of the Dodgers’ most highly regarded prospects. His journey was shaped by encouragement, Dominican family roots and decisions that helped him keep developing his talent.
Details on Josue De Paula’s MLB debut and family support
De Paula made his big league debut in the Dodgers’ 6-2 win over the Marlins. He batted seventh as the designated hitter, flying out in his first at-bat and later walking. His first appearance didn't produce a hit, but it was the start of his career at baseball's highest level.
The promotion was a surprise. De Paula was playing for the Double-A Tulsa Drillers and was called up directly to the majors, skipping Triple-A. The Dodgers added him to the roster while Shohei Ohtani was sidelined, giving the young outfielder a chance to get to the big-league roster.
How Josue De Paula’s father fueled his MLB dream
Josue De Paula Sr. has encouraged his son’s baseball aspirations since the time Josue De Paula Sr.’s son was 4 years old. The debut was particularly meaningful due to their shared connection to the sport. De Paula Sr. told MLB.com that it was an unforgettable moment that he was still processing emotionally. The hug between father and son before the game encapsulated the importance of years of support and anticipation.
The family’s baseball odyssey also included a major move during the COVID-19 pandemic. With schools closed in Brooklyn, De Paula moved to the Dominican Republic to stay with his uncles and keep training. He went to El Niche Baseball Academy in Santo Domingo before signing as an international amateur with the Dodgers in 2022. His father’s Dominican roots gave added significance to the young player’s progress.
Josue De Paula’s Dodgers rise followed family sacrifices
De Paula’s promotion came after a standout season for Tulsa. In 124 Double-A games in 2026, he hit .303 with 27 home runs, 104 RBIs and a.948 OPS. Those numbers helped make him one of the Dodgers’ most promising young hitters and supported the decision to bring him straight to the major leagues.
His grandmother, Sixtra Brito De Paula, has been an important link to Dominican culture and family. As a child, she recalled that he often carried a baseball bat, according to MLB.com. She also said she cooked traditional Dominican food during his visits and spent time with him.
Her memories hinted at the family life behind his professional success.
Josue De Paula’s debut marked a family milestone
Family members who had watched him develop long before the Dodgers promoted him shared in his first big league appearance. The debut was a personal milestone as well as a professional one, with his father's journey to Miami and his grandmother's presence there.
For the Dodgers, De Paula’s promotion presented an opportunity to evaluate a young hitter after his productive minor league season. For his family, it was the culmination of years of encouragement, training and patience, and his MLB journey is still developing, but his debut made it clear that his progress has been supported by more than just individual talent. Sixtra Brito De Paula and Josue De Paula Sr.'s presence proved how strong family still is in his path in baseball.

item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Patience and some unexpected power have the Milwaukee Brewers on the brink of their first World Series appearance in 44 years, and they will get their first chance to advance in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday. Jake Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer on Wednesday as the Brewers finished off a 6-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3. Milwaukee has a commanding 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series entering the Thur
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Patience and some unexpected power have the Milwaukee Brewers on the brink of their first World Series appearance in 44 years, and they will get their first chance to advance in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday.
Jake Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer on Wednesday as the Brewers finished off a 6-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3.
Milwaukee has a commanding 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series entering the Thursday contest at Dodger Stadium.
Bauers' tenacity was so complete that on-deck hitter Garrett Mitchell went to the plate inspired. He added his own home run, giving a team that rarely used might this season its third home run of the game.
"Super sick," Mitchell said of the at-bat by Bauers. "He's trying to move the guy over, and (he) put an incredible swing on that. For me being able to watch that on deck was awesome."
The power display came after the Brewers hit 154 home runs in the regular season. Only the Toronto Blue Jays had fewer in the major leagues with 152.
"We play for each other," Bauers said. "When you have 26 guys that are bought into that and believe that and show up every day, completely selfless, playing for each other, it's a special thing to be a part of."
Milwaukee announced Thursday that rookie left-hander Shane Drohan will get the start as the team attempts to complete a sweep that would avenge their sweep at the hands of Los Angeles in last year's NLCS.
Advertisement
Drohan will be making his postseason debut. He was 7-5 with a 4.19 ERA and two saves in 33 games (19 starts) in the regular season. He faced the Dodgers three times (one start) and had no decisions with a 4.66 ERA, striking out 12 and walking five in 9 2/3 innings.
The Dodgers will put their season on the line with Tyler Glasnow on the mound. The right-hander started the Game 4 clincher in the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves and gave up one run over 4 2/3 innings but walked five.
In nine career regular-season appearances (five starts) against the Brewers, Glasnow is 0-3 with a 4.55 ERA. He also started Game 3 of the 2025 NLCS against Milwaukee and gave up one run over 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision.
While getting Glasnow to find his command will be key, the Dodgers also need some offensive consistency. Shohei Ohtani has struggled since late in the regular season and was moved to the No. 6 spot in the order for Game 3. He came through by reaching base three times, including a hard-hit single late in the game.
Los Angeles catcher Will Smith, who had been in a 1-for-25 postseason slide, delivered a two-run double. However, the Dodgers finished with just five hits on the night after collecting just three in their Game 2 loss at Milwaukee.
"I'll talk to them (Thursday)," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of his players. "They know what's at stake. We've won four in a row a number of times this year. Ten times, I think, something like that."
And Roberts knows what a comeback from a 3-0 deficit in a league championship series looks like. His stolen base inspired the Boston Red Sox to an improbable rally over the New York Yankees in 2004. That was the only time in the previous 42 instances that a major league team escaped an 0-3 postseason hole to win a best-of-seven series.
"Our guys know how good (the Brewers) are. Our guys know what we're up against," Roberts said. "But that doesn't change anything. We come out and play the same way every time."
--Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
On Day 5 of the League Championship Series, one team broke a series tie ... will another advance to the Fall Classic?
After splitting the first two games in Tampa Bay, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays faced off at Progressive Field in the day's first game. Thanks toPetey Halpin-- and his epic bat flip -- Cleveland prevailed, taking a 2-1 ALCS lead.
Tonight, in what could be the finale of the NLCS, the Milwaukee Brewers will look to continue their dominant championship series run and sweep the reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium. Can the Dodgers stave off elimination in Game 4 -- or will the Brewers advance to their first World Series since 1982?
Stay tuned for in-game action and postgame analysis from Los Angeles and Cleveland.
Key links: How final four teams were built | Playoff MVP tracker | Schedule
Cleveland leads series 2-1
It was over when ... Petey Halpin cranked a 96 mph sinker down the middle from Griffin Jax in the fifth inning. The ball landed deep into the right-field seats, 385 feet away, for a go-ahead two-run home run. Halpin flipped his bat nearly that high, too, and Cleveland didn't look back.
Game 3 star: Halpin, who began the season in Triple-A, had four big league home runs -- all during the regular season -- in 213 career plate appearances before Thursday. The center fielder's first postseason homer was the difference Thursday.
The stat that defined the game:The Rays' 13 strikeouts against Guardians pitching. The Rays posted the lowest strikeout rate in the majors this season at 18.8%. They struck out more than 12 times once, when they compiled 14 strikeouts against the Milwaukee Brewers back on March 30 in their fourth game of the season. Rays star Junior Caminero went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts -- matching a career high from 2025. So Thursday was an extreme outlier. Guardians starter Gavin Williams, the American League's strikeout leader this season, had nine strikeouts in five innings before four relievers combined for the remaining four punchouts. Tampa Bay will have to put the ball in play more to come back and win this series.
What it means for the rest of the series: With rain in the forecast Friday, there's a chance this series won't play Game 4 until Saturday. If so, the clubs would play Game 5 on Sunday, which would take away their travel day before a potential Game 6 in Tampa Bay on Monday. For now, Game 4 is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET Friday. -- Jorge Castillo

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Max Muncy’s no-nonsense response to Dodgers’ performance doesn’t instill confidence for Game 4
item.dc:creator: Colin Keane
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting severely outplayed by the Milwaukee Brewers through the first three games of the National League Championship Series. LA's been outscored 15-7 so far in the series, and they've hit zero home runs to Milwaukee's five. In Game 3, the Dodgers managed just five hits, failing to generate enough offense to compete with the Brewers' aggressive style. Jackson Chourio went yard on the first pitch of the game from Blake Snell. When LA seized the lead back in the sixth o
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting severely outplayed by the Milwaukee Brewers through the first three games of the National League Championship Series. LA's been outscored 15-7 so far in the series, and they've hit zero home runs to Milwaukee's five.
In Game 3, the Dodgers managed just five hits, failing to generate enough offense to compete with the Brewers' aggressive style. Jackson Chourio went yard on the first pitch of the game from Blake Snell. When LA seized the lead back in the sixth on a two-run double from Will Smith, Milwaukee bounced right back: In the next half inning, Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back jacks off of Snell to re-take the lead.
The Brewers added additional runs in the eighth and ninth, whereas the Dodgers' bats didn't capitalize on opportunities to stay in the game (1-for-6 with runners in scoring position). Following the deflating result, Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy didn't exactly wax poetic about LA's struggles.
Max Muncy's blunt analysis of the Dodgers' struggles doesn't inspire faith for Game 4
Muncy's assessment of things is accurate, but it doesn't help Dodgers fans feel any better about Game 4 on Thursday night. It's admirable that Muncy chose to be honest rather than come up with some excuses for the Dodgers, but doing so also reinforced the harsh reality that LA simply might not be good enough right now to overcome what looks like a team of destiny over in the Brewers' dugout.
And there aren't excuses to make -- the Dodgers' stars are present, just not performing. Shohei Ohtani hasn't been himself, and it's not like LA's offense is without proven playoff performers like Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman at the moment. Muncy's not helping matters, either, at least not in this series. After an awesome NLDS, Muncy is 1-for-9 with four strikeouts so far in the NLCS.
To keep their three-peat dream alive, the Dodgers must make history
If Muncy sounds pessimistic, it's probably because he understands the history of baseball. Only one team (the 2004 Boston Red Sox) has ever come back and won a best-of-seven series after trailing 3-0. It's never been done in an NLCS. If there's a group with the talent required to pull off the near-impossible, it's these Dodgers, but talent might not be the issue here.
The problem is momentum. The Brewers have scores of it, whereas the Dodgers look stuck in the mud. The other issue is that LA doesn't have any runway to generate the momentum they need. They are in the middle of a series and must act immediately or watch their season and three-peat hopes end just as swiftly.
Tyler Glasnow will surely put in a good performance in Game 4, but it won't mean anything if the Dodgers' offense is weak yet again. Muncy's simple assessment of things leads to a simple directive for the Dodgers: get on base early and often, and drive guys in when you do.

item.title: [New York Post] Brewers vs. Dodgers Game 4 prediction: NLCS picks, odds, bets
item.dc:creator: Sean Treppedi
item.description: The Brewers’ stunning 3-0 stranglehold on the Dodgers in the NLCS is the epitome of there being no guarantees in sports. Milwaukee has several feats in front of them when they take the field for Game 4 on Thursday evening. Firstly, the Brewers can slay the Los Angeles beast that has won back-to-back titles and outspends them by $193.1 million on their roster. Beyond that, they can end a 44-year World Series drought and become the first club in history to sweep an opponent the following year afte
item.content:encoded:
The Brewers’ stunning 3-0 stranglehold on the Dodgers in the NLCS is the epitome of there being no guarantees in sports.
Milwaukee has several feats in front of them when they take the field for Game 4 on Thursday evening.
Firstly, the Brewers can slay the Los Angeles beast that has won back-to-back titles and outspends them by $193.1 million on their roster. Beyond that, they can end a 44-year World Series drought and become the first club in history to sweep an opponent the following year after getting swept by that same team.
Brewers vs. Dodgers Game 4 prediction, best bet
Narratives aside, Milwaukee has simply been the better team in all facets.
Their plate discipline has worn down the Dodgers’ all-world pitching staff by forcing pitchers into prolonged at-bats and pouncing on mistakes. The Brewers have drawn 13 walks in this series.
For all the power hitting the Dodgers deploy, the Brewers own a staggering .458-to-.187 advantage in slugging percentage.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy has masterfully mixed and matched his pitching staff, and it’s helped produce a postseason-best 1.74 ERA.
This is a team built on role players, and their collective execution has far outweighed financial might and market size.
In order to advance, the Brewers will have to solve Tyler Glasnow, who owns a 1.73 ERA across 26 career postseason innings and has helped the Dodgers go 7-0 in games he’s pitched. Fortunately, for Milwaukee, command was a problem in the NLDS, having walked five Braves hitters.
Glasnow’s effectiveness has waned since his Aug. 25 return from a three-and-a-half-month absence due to back spasms. He’s managed a 4.15 ERA across 39 innings since Aug. 25, with his Stuff+ dipping to 98, per FanGraphs.
The Brewers will counter with rookie left-hander Shane Drohan, who hasn’t pitched since Sept. 27, before potentially turning to former Dodger Dustin May for bulk innings.
While it’s hardly an intimidating arrangement on paper, the bullpen has allowed just one earned run over 28 ⅔ innings.

The Dodgers would need to crack that with a lineup that has batted .165 with a .187 slugging percentage in the series. And, oh yeah, they’re sticking with Shohei Ohtani, whose perseverance through injuries has made for a .182 average through seven postseason games and no home runs since Aug. 18.
Oddsmakers expect a response from the Dodgers, tagging the Brewers at +130 to win. Follow the evidence and take them to complete the sweep and cash another underdog ticket.
THE PLAY: Brewers (+135, Caesars)

item.content:encoded:
米メディア『ドジャース・ウェイ』は13日（日本時間14日）、「『大谷翔平は投手をやめるべきか』という議論が現実味を帯びてきた」と題して記事を公開。「ユニコーンとしての地位は間もなく終わりを迎えるかもしれない」とし、身体的負担の大きい二刀流を続けることが可能か、疑問の声が高まっている現状を伝えた。
■打者専念も……ポストシーズン絶不調
左膝痛、首周りの不調、右上腕二頭筋の炎症などを抱え、9月上旬に負傷者リスト入りした大谷。復帰後は今シーズン中の「二刀流」を断念し、打者に専念すると表明した。それでも完全回復には至っておらず、その影響からかレギュラーシーズン終盤からポストシーズンにかけて極度の打撃不振に陥っている。
そこで『ドジャース・ウェイ』は、「根本的な問題として、大谷は投手としてのキャリアを終える時が来たのだろうか」と投げ掛けた。
同メディアは記事の中で、米ポッドキャスト番組『ファウル・テリトリー』で司会を務めるA.J.ピアジンスキー氏のコメントを紹介。同氏はナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズでドジャースが連敗した直後、同番組内で大谷に対する見解を述べた。
「ある朝、彼は目を覚まして『もう投手はやらない』と言うかもしれない」とし、それは早ければ来年訪れてもおかしくないと主張した。
■あと何年投げられる？
さらに「私は、彼とチームが契約した時に『あと何年で投げられなくなるのか』と疑問を提示したんだ」とし、この元メジャーリーグ捕手は以前から二刀流の“寿命”に注目していたと明かした。その上で「投手を続けることで得られるものが、そのための負担に見合うのか、近いうちに問う必要があるだろう」と指摘した。
投打を担うことで生じる負担と打撃への影響が改めて議論の的となっているが、『ドジャース・ウェイ』は「現在の打撃不振を二刀流の負担というだけで説明できるのか。投手をやめるべきだという結論も、外部から一方的に下せるものではない。今後の起用法は、大谷本人とデーブ・ロバーツ監督、アンドリュー・フリードマン編成本部長らが協議すべき課題である」とした。
大谷の二刀流を支えつつ、どう疲労や故障を抑え、どう能力を引き出すか。『ドジャース・ウェイ』は「ピアジンスキー氏の“負担に見合うのか”という問いは、来季以降の起用を考える上で重い論点になりそうだ」と締めくくった。

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ blasts on brink of World Series

MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ bl
item.content:encoded:
Is this finally the year the Brewers exorcise their playoff demons and advance past the Dodgers on the Senior Circuit side of the bracket? Alongside LA, Milwaukee has been the class of the NL regular season for the last decade. However, they have never beaten their postseason final boss during this era, getting eliminated by the Dodgers in seven games in the instant classic 2018 NLCS before getting swept in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series and 2025 NLCS.
MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ blasts on brink of World Series
Milwaukee is on the cusp of sweeping the Dodgers and making their second World Series appearance in franchise history.
That finally looks set to change, the Brewers taking a commanding 3-0 lead in the series on a brilliant start from Robert Gasser and home runs from Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, and Garrett Mitchell. With one more win, they’ll not only avenge those losses, but also win their first pennant in 44 years, when Harvey’s Wallbangers led the 1982 Brewers to the AL flag. Only the Pirates and Mariners have waited longer for a World Series berth. Could this be the year at last for dreams of a first Brewers championship to truly ignite?
They have one more win to go. Here’s how they got to the doorstep.
NLCS Game 3
Milwaukee Brewers 5, Los Angeles Dodgers 2
(Milwaukee leads, 3-0)
There is no better start to the game as a visiting team than a leadoff home run to put the home starter and crowd immediately on the back foot. Chourio said “hold my beer” as he homered on the first pitch of Game 3, ambushing a center-cut four-seamer from Blake Snell and lining it oppo just over the wall in right-center to instantly deflate a raucous crowd at Chavez Ravine who had been desperate to energize their wounded Dodgers. It is already the third postseason leadoff home run in the young career of the Brewers’ star left fielder, Chourio the hero of the NLDS against the Padres with six RBIs in four games.
Gasser typifies a Milwaukee Brewers player — a gamer with plenty of talent but not a name a baseball fan outside of Wisconsin is likely to recognize. He was part of the 2022 deadline trade that sent Josh Hader to San Diego. He debuted in 2024 but missed most of that and the next season to Tommy John surgery. He spent the first month-and-a-half of 2026 at Triple-A but didn’t look back after a mid-May call-up, starting 20 games and posting a 5-5 record, 3.87 ERA, 4.23 FIP, 103 strikeouts and 1.5 fWAR in 109.1 innings.
With the Brewers unsettled on their postseason rotation plans, Gasser allowed one or fewer runs in his final four starts of the regular season to cement his starting role in the playoffs. The 27-year-old lefty held the Padres to a run on three hits in four innings of Game 4 of the NLDS as the Brewers punched their ticket to the next round. Against this backdrop of hitting his stride once the games really started to matter, Gasser pitched possibly the best start of his life last night.
He’s not going to blow you away with velocity, but the unique way he hides the ball until the last moment of his delivery let his mid-90s sinker play up in LA. The Dodgers had no answer for the pitch as Gasser was able to paint both sides of the plate, getting the ball by the dangerous hitters in their lineup as if they collectively were not ready to hit the fastball.
Gasser waltzed through five scoreless innings allowing just three hits and a walk, but cameras curiously spotted handshakes in the dugout between the fifth and sixth innings. Gasser hadn’t had to make a stressful pitch all game and seemed to have plenty in the tank at just 72 pitches, but trainers did appear to be tending to a blister on the ring finger of his pitching hand. Practically every button that Brewers manager Pat Murphy has pushed this season and postseason has worked, seeing the team pace MLB with 103 wins and easily brush aside the Padres in the NLDS before taking a 2-0 lead over the two-time reigning champions, but this one blew up in his face.
Whatever the case, Murphy called on Abner Uribe for the sixth inning and it backfired spectacularly. He walked Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker, and Shohei Ohtani (batting a rare sixth amid his awful slump) to load the bases with one out. Despite a pair of relievers hot in the Milwaukee bullpen, Murphy allowed Uribe to face the struggling Will Smith — 1-for-23 in six games this postseason. Smith ambushed a first pitch sinker right down the pipe, the deep fly ball clanging halfway up the wall in left-center to plate a pair and give the Dodgers their first lead of the series, 2-1.
Murphy belatedly called on flame throwing lefty DL Hall to clean up Uribe’s mess, and he struck out Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman to strand runners on second and third and limit the damage to the two runs.
Murphy was perhaps vindicated in lifting his starter earlier than it seemed necessary, because we witnessed the flip side of that debate two innings later. It is perhaps fitting that Snell was the starter opposite Gasser in this game —the Rays’ Kevin Cash memorably removed Snell in the sixth inning of Game 6 of the 2020 World Series against the Dodgers despite Snell having struck out nine and not allowed a run on just 73 pitches — Gasser removed with his pitch count at 72.
After the Chourio leadoff blast, Snell was untouchable for six innings, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out nine as his four-seamer had some extra juice en route to racking up a gaudy 46-percent whiff rate. Dave Roberts allowed his dominating starter to come back out for the seventh, and it is amazing how the tide turned in an instant. He issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn, but with two lefties due up in Bauers and Mitchell, Roberts stuck with his southpaw starter.
The fatigue was apparent against Bauers, Snell’s misses occurring over the heart of the plate instead of outside of the zone, and the Brewers’ regular season home run leader won the monumental 11-pitch battle by blasting a middle-middle full count four-seamer 412 feet to right to put the Brewers back on top, 3-2. Mitchell then jumped on a 1-0 mistake changeup right down the middle, going back-to-back with Bauers to almost the exact same spot of the ballpark.
It was the first time in Snell’s entire career that he had allowed back-to-back homers to lefties and just the second time that he’d ever allowed two lefty-hitter homers in the same game (let alone inning). He’d allowed one lefty-hitter homer since Juan Soto took him deep for the Yankees in June 2024 in San Francisco.
That fully sucked all of the air out of Dodger Stadium, and the team nor their fans could will the comeback. Milwaukee added a pair of valuable insurance runs in the eighth and ninth. Brice Turang and William Contreras reached in the eighth on consecutive one-out singles to put runners on the corners where a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch allowed Turang to score the Brewers’ fifth run. Rookie Cooper Pratt lined a one-out single in the ninth, stole second, and scored on a Joey Ortiz single to make it 6-2. Hall and closer Trevor Megill combined to pitch a scoreless final 3.2 innings to seal the win and put the Brewers on the brink of sweeping the champions of the last two seasons.
Game 4 is tomorrow with first pitch scheduled for 8:00 pm ET. Tyler Glasnow will look to keep the Dodgers’ season alive while Milwaukee has yet to name a starter. The Brewers now have four chances to clinch the series and advance to the Fall Classic, where they will look to win their first ever title as one of five teams to have never won a ring. No expansion team has waited longer. It may finally be the Brew Crew’s year.

"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a
item.content:encoded:
NEED TO KNOW
- Alex Call is taking issue with suggestive ads that air during MLB games
- The Dodgers outfielder shared his outrage on X in a post
- "Parents shouldn't have to worry about this," Call, who is not on the team's postseason roster, said
Alex Call is calling foul on recent commercials that he says feature "half-naked women."
"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a post discussing the trend. "My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America's Pastime. Parents shouldn't have to worry about this."
Call's response was to a post in which a Utah-based X user shared his displeasure with commercials that star Sydney Sweeney and Megan Fox.
Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this. https://t.co/7YAWSZgo5d
— Alex Call (@ACAD_27) October 14, 2026
In addition to the 32-year-old outfielder, female athletes are among those outraged by Sweeney's sports-betting ad for Novig.
In the commercials, the Euphoria actress, 29, bares almost all while posing in provocative positions.
"Just you, your takes and sports," Sweeney, topless and holding her breasts, says into the camera.
Call — who was left off the Dodgers' postseason roster — has had time to watch games at home with his family amid the team's playoff run.
The right fielder also made headlines earlier this season for his position — in which he nearly injured Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani.
In July, Call clipped Ohtani's right elbow with his cleat while jumping over the dugout railing to celebrate the team's win against the Philadelphia Phillies.
Ohtani, 32, briefly clutched his elbow before the two players laughed off the near-miss.
Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!
On Wednesday night, the designated hitter managed a single in two at bats amid a self-owned slump triggered by lingering injuries.
"The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit," Ohtani told reporters through his interpreter on Tuesday, Oct. 13. "The results, [I] take full responsibility."
The Dodgers will try to stave off elimination on Friday, Oct. 16 for Game 5, when they face the Milwaukee Brewers, who will earn a trip to the World Series with a win.

item.title: [1069thefox.com] Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and ride 6-2 win to 3-0 lead in NLCS - 106.9 The Fox
item.dc:creator: Schristian

Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Jackson Chourio als
item.content:encoded:
By BETH HARRIS AP Sports Writer
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Milwaukee Brewers hit the second-fewest home runs in baseball during the regular season, even as they topped the majors with 103 wins.
Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell launched back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to build a 3-0 cushion in the National League Championship Series.
Jackson Chourio also went deep on the first pitch of the game to help the Brewers close within one win of their first NL pennant. Milwaukee was in the American League when the franchise reached its only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason.
Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.
The Dodgers had just gone ahead 2-1 in the sixth inning before getting stunned by the Brewers in their three-run seventh. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.
“All three games we’ve played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score,” Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said. “That’s not easy to do in baseball.”
It was the fifth comeback victory in seven postseason games for the Brewers, who have never beaten Los Angeles in three previous playoff series.
The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “We’ve got to win tomorrow. That’s our only focus.”
Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. But the first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell’s solo shot.
Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the seventh and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of his at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee’s dugout came onto the field to celebrate.
“I was looking for a fastball, and I didn’t want to miss it,” said Bauers, who had a team-leading 26 of Milwaukee’s 154 regular-season homers.
It was his latest relentless plate appearance, too, after Bauers drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.
“I think what changed for me this year was I stopped caring about results,” Bauers said. “I started caring about competing. I started caring about being in the moment and getting out of my own way.”
Watching Bauers work over Snell was “super sick,” Mitchell said.
And then it was his turn.
Mitchell’s drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn’t given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was the first time in his career he served up back-to-back homers to left-handed hitters and only the second time he gave up multiple longballs to left-handed batters in one game.
Bauers and Mitchell became just the third pair of left-handed hitters with consecutive postseason home runs off the same left-handed pitcher. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper did it for Philadelphia against Atlanta reliever Dylan Lee in an NL Wild Card Series this year, and Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig connected for the New York Yankees off Bill Sherdel of the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1928 World Series.
Milwaukee has five homers in the NLCS and eight this postseason.
Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six-plus innings. He struck out nine and walked two.
The Brewers extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski’s wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras’ single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz’s two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers took a 2-1 lead on Will Smith’s two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.
After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.
Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.
The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer in the postseason as fans were still heading to their seats.
After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.
The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn’t get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS and are 3 for 32 with runners in scoring position this postseason.
Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he’s batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here

item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs. Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a sta
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs.
Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a starter, all signs point towards Dustin May taking the ball in Game 4 of this series—it might be with an opener, or it might be with him as a starter; either way, the bulk innings role will belong to the former Dodger.
When it comes to lineup decisions, Max Muncy figures to regain a starting role at third base, and you have to wonder if Will Smith remains in the seventh spot—the Dodger catcher was responsible for the only big hit the home team had in a Game 3 loss. Speaking of hitters who moved down in the order, although it amounted to very little, Shohei Ohtani reached safely in three of his four plate appearances in a 6-2 defeat.
Neither Evan Phillips nor Roki Sasaki had especially lengthy appearances off the bullpen, so apart from Justin Wrobleski, there’ll be no one else unavailable in the bullpen for Game 4. With nothing to lose and following the seventh-inning debacle of leaving Blake Snell in too long, expect potential aggressive calls to the bullpen at the first sign of trouble for Glasnow.
NLCS Game 4 info
- Teams: No. 2 seed Dodgers vs. No. 1 seed Brewers
- Series: Milwaukee leads, 3-0
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles
- Start time: 5:08 p.m.
- TV: FS1 (Joe Davis, John Smoltz, Ken Rosenthal, Tom Verducci)
- National radio: ESPN Radio (Jon Sciambi, Doug Glanville)
- Local English radio: AM 570 (Charley Steiner, Rick Monday)
- Local Spanish radio: KTNQ 1020 AM (José Mota, Luis Cruz)

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Max Muncy Puts Dodgers' Problems Plainly
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is. Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning. Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is.
Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning.
Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers
Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive struggles, and he pulled no punches.
“It’s a pretty simple answer. We’re playing like s—. They’re playing great,” he said, as reported by the California Post’s Jack Harris and other reporters.
In case you think Muncy is being hyperbolic, he’s not.
As detailed by Newsweek baseball writer J.P. Hoornstra, the Dodgers are one of 274 teams too play at least seven postseason games in a season since 1903.
Their team OPS of .572 isn’t just in the lower end of that group; it’s almost dead last.
The 2026 Dodgers are 268th, meaning only six teams have had a worse OPS in more than a century.
It’s a far cry from the powerful lineup fans expected from the back-to-back World Series champions.
In fact, the Dodgers haven’t hit a home run at all in this series against the Brewers, despite boasting power hitters like Muncy, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and plenty of others.
What’s next for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers will try to avoid “playing like s—” for a fourth straight game on Thursday, knowing that a loss will end their season.
Tyler Glasnow is the mound for the Boys in Blue as they look to avoid the sweep.
The game will begin at 5 p.m. PT, an hour earlier than the previously announced start time of 6 p.m. PT.
Pitcher Blake Snell, who started Game 3 and gave up a pair of back-breaking home runs in the seventh inning, told reporters the team is focused on winning Thursday’s game.
“Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it,” he said. “How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”
Do you think the Dodgers can stave off elimination on Thursday?

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Max Muncy gives blunt assessment of Dodgers' performance vs. Brewers in NLCS: 'We're playing like s***'
item.dc:creator: Chris Cwik
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason. This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on. When asked
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason.
This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on.
When asked, Muncy summed things up succinctly saying, "We're playing like s***."
"It's a pretty simple answer: We're playing like s*** they're playing great."
Max Muncy after the Dodgers dropped Game 3 of the NLCS. pic.twitter.com/0MRmqhpnDk
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 15, 2026
Muncy, of course, made sure to give the Milwaukee Brewers credit. After lamenting his own team's struggles, Muncy added, "[The Brewers] are playing great. It's as simple as that."
Much has been made of the struggles of Dodgers two-way star Shohei Ohtani this postseason, but he wasn't the problem Wednesday. After being dropped to sixth in the batting order, Ohtani reached base three times in the contest.
His overall numbers, however, are still a problem, as Ohtani is hitting just .182 in the series. Many of his teammates have similar batting averages, including Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernandez and Muncy, none of whom is hitting above .192. Catcher Will Smith is hitting under .100.
While those struggles can be written off as small-sample outcomes … the NLCS is a small sample. All it takes is a few bad games from your star players to decide the outcome of a series. The Dodgers are experiencing that phenomenon right now.
Because of that, though, it won't take much for the Dodgers to claw their way back into the series. While 3-0 comebacks are highly unlikely, they are not impossible. All it would take is the Dodgers' stars hitting like they should.
Even then, that might not be enough. In order to stage a comeback, the Dodgers also need the Brewers to give them an opening, which seems unlikely given how well Milwaukee is playing right now.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグのポストシーズン中継のテレビ広告が過激だとSNSで批判したドジャースのアレックス・コール外野手（32）が14日（日本時間15日）、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ第3戦の行われたドジャーススタジアムで声援を浴びた。
コールは13日、自身のSNSに「プレーオフの放送から『ソフトポルノ』のような広告を排除してくれないか」と投稿。「息子が父親と一緒に野球を見たがっている。だが、いつ画面に半裸の女性が映るかわからない状況を、どう子供に説明すればいいというのか。野球はアメリカの娯楽（過去の古き良き伝統）だ。親がこんな心配をすべきではない」と訴えた。
TBS、Fox、NBCなどの米テレビ局のポストシーズン中継のイニング間には、人気女優のシドニー・スウィーニーが出演するスポーツベットアプリ「Novig」のCMが繰り返し流れている。スウィーニーはアメフトのボール2個で胸元を隠すのみの姿で登場したり、バスケットゴールの上に全裸に近い状態で着座するなどの演出がある。
また、別のオンライン診療サービスのCMでは、女優ミーガン・フォックスが赤いボディースーツ姿で男性用医薬品「Ro Sparks」を宣伝しているほか、刺激の強いホラー映画の予告編なども同時間帯に放映されている。
コールの投稿をきっかけにネット上で論争が起き、「その広告収入が君たちの年俸を支えている」といった冷ややかな声も。一方、ブレーブスで2度の最優秀選手（MVP）に輝いたレジェンド、デール・マーフィー氏はコールと同様の意見をSNSに投稿した。
Novigは、株のようにスポーツの試合結果を金融商品として取引するアプリ。胴元（カジノ会社）が存在せず、ユーザー同士で取引が行われる。

item.title: [KTVN] Shohei Ohtani batting 6th, a lone single, and the Dodgers staring at playoff elimination

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Slumping star Shohei Ohtani singled after being dropped to sixth in the batting order for the Los Angeles Dodgers, whose 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series put them on the brink of postseason elimination Wednesday night.
It's the lowest the left-handed-hitting Ohtani has batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago on a $700 million, 10-year contract. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts wanted to alternate right- and left-handed hitters throughout the lineup against Milwaukee's left-handed starter, Robert Gasser.
”Shohei’s all on board," Roberts said before the game. “Whatever it takes to win.”
It wasn't enough, and now the two-time defending World Series champions trail 3-0 in the best-of-seven series.
Ohtani flied out in the second inning, got hit by a pitch in the fourth and walked in the sixth before singling with two outs in the eighth. The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings.
“We’re just not getting those timely hits,” Roberts said afterward. “We’ve had some opportunities with guys on base, but can’t get that hit.”
Ohtani, the designated hitter, is typically atop the order, but Roberts has dropped him lower during a slump that has extended into the postseason. Ohtani has been struggling with left knee and right biceps issues for a few months, preventing the two-way star from pitching, and said before the Division Series against Atlanta that he wasn't 100% healthy.
During his six years with the Los Angeles Angels, Ohtani started games batting sixth or lower 19 times, all during the 2020 season or earlier.
Ohtani is hitting .182 (4 for 22) over seven postseason games. He has seven strikeouts, four walks and one stolen base with no RBIs and an OPS of .533.
He hasn’t homered since Aug. 18 at Colorado.
“I couldn’t imagine really kind of having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” teammate Mookie Betts said before the game. “Then having to come back and be present in this postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
Roberts said he saw a more focused Ohtani during off-day batting practice Tuesday.
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement,” the manager said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things on how we're going to beat these guys.”
Dodgers pitcher Tyler Glasnow, set to start Game 4 on Thursday, said Ohtani's demeanor doesn't deviate regardless of how well he's performing.
“I think most people put in that situation, you’d have a lot more emotional volatility, so it’s just impressive to see him just be a good dude always,” Glasnow said. “I don’t think he needs reassurance or anything. He’s confident in himself. It’s just business as usual and a lot of smiles and the same laugh.”

The Dodgers dropped Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday, leaving them with a massive deficit to overcome. No National League team has ever come back from a 3-0 margin in the championship series, so history is not on Los Angeles' side.
Starting pitcher Blake Snell gave up four runs, and star Shohei Ohtani wasn't able to manage more than a single amid his ongoing struggles. The Brewers, meanwhile, homered three times to keep the momentum on their side.

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
Blake Snell stood on the mound with his hand on his hip, waiting for Jake Bauers to cross the plate before punching in his pitch call for the next batter.
The Dodgers left-hander had just given up the lead on Bauers’ two-run homer, spoiling what had been a stellar start Wednesday night at Dodger Stadium. But Snell was ready to move on.
Two pitches later, he watched another ball fly over the fence, this time off Garrett Mitchell’s bat.
The Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, after the visitors regained the lead with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning, gave the Brewers a commanding 3-0 lead and set up an elimination game Thursday. After setting their sights on a history-making three-peat, the Dodgers will have to win the next four games just to advance to the World Series.
The Dodgers showed signs of life during Game 3 of the NLCS, but Bill Plaschke writes the reigning champs can’t survive their crushing collapse.
For five innings, the only run on the board was the one the Brewers scored on the first pitch of the game.
Snell zipped a 97.6-mph fastball over the center of the plate, and Brewers leadoff hitter Jackson Chourio sent it into the first row of the stands in right-center.
For much of Snell’s start, however, that aggressive approach worked. He dotted the upper rail with his fastball, threw his curveball for both swings and misses and called strikes, and mixed in his changeup to right-handed batters.
Unlike Snell’s last postseason start, when he issued five walks and lasted just 3-2/3 innings against the Atlanta Braves, his efficiency got him through six-plus innings Wednesday, with just two walks.
And while Snell’s fastball averaged 97 mph in his last start — something he’d done only twice before in his career, regular season or postseason, and not since 2022, according to Statcast — he threw even harder on Wednesday: 97.3 mph.
After Chourio’s home run, Snell retired 18 of the next 20 batters, including 14 in a row, to get through six innings. His nine strikeouts were one shy of a postseason career high, which he recorded against the Brewers last year in Game 1 of the NLCS.
Then in the seventh inning, he issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn and surrendered back-to-back homers, and suddenly the game had flipped.
With the way the Brewers’ bullpen pitched in the first two games, it seemed the Dodgers would have to score against the Brewers’ starters to have a chance to pull themselves out of the hole they’d dug.
They failed to do so in Game 3, logging just three hits off left-hander Robert Gasser.
Luckily for them, pitching every game of the postseason seemed to finally have caught up to hard-throwing right-handed Abner Uribe in his seventh appearance.
Uribe took over for Gasser in the sixth inning and walked the first two batters he faced.
Then Dodgers manager Dave Roberts had left-handed-hitting Max Muncy pinch-hit for Andy Pages. Muncy struck out, and the biggest moment of the game fell to two Dodgers who have had the worst postseason production on the team.
Roberts had moved Shohei Ohtani down to sixth in the batting order and put Will Smith behind him. Naturally, the game found them.
Ohtani drew a five-pitch walk without taking a swing. With the bases loaded, it was up to Smith, who had gone one for 25 in the postseason to that point.
He ambushed a first-pitch sinker and drove it into the left-field gap for a two-run double and the lead.
The rally halted there. Roberts burned rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch-hitter, swapping him out for Kiké Hernández when the Brewers brought in left-hander DL Hall. Hernández and Tommy Edman struck out to end the inning.
The Dodgers could not keep pace with the Milwaukee Brewers, falling 6-2 Wednesday night in Game 3 of the NLCS and dropping to 3-0 in the series.
Then, three Brewers batters into the seventh, the Dodgers were down 4-2.
Snell hadn’t allowed a home run all year — not in his nine regular-season starts, or in his NLDS appearance. Three on Wednesday defined his start.
The next inning, the Brewers added an insurance run with back-to-back singles against right-handed reliever Roki Sasaki and a wild pitch from left-hander Justin Wrobleski. They tacked on another in the ninth with a pair of singles and a stolen base off Wrobleski.
With the flash of red tail lights flickering outside of the stadium, a sign of Dodgers fans already heading for the exits, Dodgers hitters went down in order in the final half inning.

item.title: [FanSided] 3 mistakes the Dodgers made with their money that cost them a chance at a three-peat
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles thanks largely to historic spending. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles thanks largely to historic spending. A full14 players on the Dodgers' roster are making eight figures this season, and Tarik Skubal (who is making $32 million overall, but $9.5 million prorated after the Dodgers acquired him) isn't far behind from making that 15. For reference, the Mets, the team closest to L.A. payroll-wise, ended the year with just eight players making eight figures this season.
Most of those deals are ones the Dodgers would sign off on again. Even guys who have struggled this postseason, like Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith, have done so much for this team in recent years that it's hard to say the Dodgers should regret paying them. These three deals, though, are ones that the Dodgers should regret offering, now that their three-peat dreams are officially on life support.
OF Kyle Tucker
This is the obvious one. The Dodgers, even after winning back-to-back World Series titles, elected to give Kyle Tucker a four-year, $240 million deal in free agency. When that deal was signed, most MLB fans practically handed the World Series title to L.A., knowing how good Tucker had been in Houston. Instead, Tucker wound up having the worst year of his career.
He slashed .233/.330/.385 with 17 home runs and 70 RBI. He was better down the stretch and has been arguably their best hitter in the postseason, but he's just 2-for-8 in the NLCS. That's not good enough for a player making $60 million a year on average. For reference, Juan Soto's AAV is at $51 million, and he's performed at an MVP level. If the Dodgers got to do it again, they almost certainly wouldn't have made this kind of investment in Tucker.
RHP Edwin Diaz
Tucker wasn't the only high-end free agent the Dodgers signed. They gave Edwin Diaz a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, one year after giving Tanner Scott a four-year, $72 million deal to perform in that same role. Scott's first year in L.A. was one to forget, and Diaz followed that same path, posting an 8.68 ERA in 21 games and missing much of the season due to injury.
Diaz was better in the postseason, but given how well Scott performed this season and how lackluster this Dodgers lineup proved to be, wouldn't Andrew Friedman have preferred to give that kind of major money to a big bat? Hindsight is 20/20, but had they known the offense would look this bad in October, they likely would've spent their resources on another bat and let Diaz sign elsewhere.
OF Teoscar Hernandez
Teoscar Hernandez had a huge year in 2024, leading to the Dodgers re-signing him on a three-year, $66 million deal that offseason. That contract made some sense, but handing a power-hitting corner outfielder over the age of 30 a hefty multi-year deal has the risk of backfiring — and this one did almost immediately. Hernandez's 103 OPS+ in 2025 was his worst in a full season in his career, and while he was a bit better overall in 2026, his streakiness and his numbers against righties (.695 OPS) left a lot to be desired.
Those struggles have continued into the playoffs, with Hernandez going 5-for-26 overall and 2-for-10 in the NLCS thus far. Dave Roberts has consistently hit him in the heart of the Dodgers' order, but Hernandez has not been able to come through. There're plenty of other players making the $20+ million that Hernandez is who could've come through for L.A. offensively. With another guaranteed year on his deal, this contract feels like another one that the Dodgers regret.

item.title: [New York Post] Mookie Betts could be the answer to the Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani problem
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Before the Dodgers became Shohei Ohtani’s team, they were Mookie Betts’ team. Manager Dave Roberts used to say that as Betts went, the Dodgers went. Betts was the best player on the 2020 championship team. He finished in the top five in National League MVP voting three of his first four seasons with the Dodgers. Now, with the Dodgers trailing the Brewers in the National League Championship Series and unable to count on a physically-limited Ohtani to jumpstart their offense, Betts will have to tu
item.content:encoded:
Before the Dodgers became Shohei Ohtani’s team, they were Mookie Betts’ team.
Manager Dave Roberts used to say that as Betts went, the Dodgers went.
Betts was the best player on the 2020 championship team. He finished in the top five in National League MVP voting three of his first four seasons with the Dodgers.
Now, with the Dodgers trailing the Brewers in the National League Championship Series and unable to count on a physically-limited Ohtani to jumpstart their offense, Betts will have to turn back the clock.
The Dodgers scored only once in the first game of the NLCS and each of the four runs they scored in the second game was the result of an error or wild pitch by the Brewers, but Betts can’t be faulted for the lack of run production.
Betts, who replaced Ohtani as the leadoff hitter last month while the four-time MVP was on the injured list, was 2-for-7 through the first two games of the NLCS.
He reached base four times in nine plate appearances.
“Mookie’s at-bats at the top, and what he’s done over the last couple months has been very consistent,” Roberts said. “It’s at-bat quality at the highest level.”
The effect of those at-bats on the Dodgers’ other hitters was particularly obvious in a victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of their NL Division Series.
In his first at-bat against Braves ace Chris Sale, Betts laid off a slider that just missed the lower outside corner of the plate to work the count full. On the next pitch Betts reached base on an infield single.
“Really just trying to have good at-bats and try to not have a bunch of empty one-out flyouts,” Betts said.
The Dodgers forced Sale to throw 24 pitches in the first inning. By the end of the third inning, Sale’s pitch count was already at 69. In the fourth inning, the Dodgers struck, with home runs by Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman moving them in front, 3-0.
The Dodgers went on to win the game, 3-1, and Betts finished with two hits.
“When you’re getting into a playoff series and you get that first hitter seeing pitches, it sets the tone for the rest of the lineup, and also for that starting pitcher that it’s going to be a grindy day,” Roberts said.
Against the Brewers, the Dodgers face an entirely different kind of challenge. The strength of the Brewers is their bullpen.
“I don’t know that it’s super imperative for us to run up the pitch counts or anything because the back end of their bullpen is arguably better than everybody on the team,” Betts said. “Getting to them isn’t necessarily a huge success.”
Unless Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski is pitching for the Brewers, the Dodgers’ prime scoring opportunities to score could be against their starting pitchers.
“Really scoring runs when you can,” Betts said.
Betts described the Dodgers as being in a good headspace.
“Nobody is really panicking or anything,” he said. “Obviously we know it’s a tough task. It’s a really good ball club over there. We just have to start one game, one pitch at a time.”
Betts said he didn’t see a reason for the team to be discouraged.
“It’s not like we’re playing really bad,” he said. “I think we’re just not getting the hits that we need to really explode as an offense. One hit can kind of lead to two and then kind of keep us going.”
The Dodgers were also in trouble in each of their last two World Series runs – they were behind two-games-to-one against the San Diego Padres in their best-of-five NL Division Series in 2024; and they trailed three games to two against the Toronto Blue Jays in the World Series last year.
“I think just having that experience, that’s kind of what gives us encouragement,” Betts said. “Being that we’ve been here before and we got out of it keeps us in a really good head space.
“Obviously, every year is different, but the same rules apply. We’ve got to just keep playing the game, and that’s really it.”

item.content:encoded:
Over 10.7 million fans watched the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Fox and Fox Deportes on Sunday.
Per FOX Sports PR, that marked the most-watched opening League Championship Series game since 2005.
TOP NEWS
New Truths from NLCS, ALCS 🧐
Brewers Beat Dodgers in Game 1
Brewers Up 2-0 on Dodgers in NLCS 🍻
Game 1 was also the most-watched LCS telecast since 2010.
The last time an LCS Game 1 had more than 10.7 million viewers was Oct. 12, 2005 per Sports Media Watch. A total of 13.51 million viewers saw the St. Louis Cardinals take down the Houston Astros 5-3 in Game 1 of the NLCS.
The last time any LCS game had more than 10.7 million viewers was on Oct. 23, 2010, when the San Francisco Giants beat the Philadelphia Phillies 3-2 in Game 6 of the NLCS.
This year's NLCS brings plenty of intrigue. The Brewers won a league-high 103 games, and they're playing the back-to-back World Series champions, who won 100 games themselves. It's a matchup of the league's two best teams (record-wise) on paper.
Milwaukee is also looking for its first-ever World Series victory, while L.A. is seeking the first World Series three-peat since 1998-2000 (New York Yankees).
There's also plenty of star power, including the game's biggest global star, Dodgers DH/pitcher Shohei Ohtani. Other players include likely NL Cy Young winner (and Brewers ace) Jacob Misiorowski, scorching-hot Brewers catcher William Contreras (three homers in six playoffs games) and Dodgers stars Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman.
Milwaukee began the series by winning both games at home: 2-1 and 7-4. Brice Turang and Contreras have paced the Brewers offense with three hits and a homer apiece.
